title: From “Traffic Harvesting” to “Value Coexistence”: The Digital Paradox and Strategic Reconstruction of Temu’s Cross-border Expansion
source: Scientific Journal of Economics and Management Research
summary: In the context of the digital economy, the globalization of China’s cross-border e-commerce platforms has entered a deep transformation zone of high-quality development. Temu, leveraging a digital ternary leverage system, has achieved explo
content: In the context of the digital economy, the globalization of China’s cross-border e-commerce platforms has entered a deep transformation zone of high-quality development. Temu, leveraging a digital ternary leverage system, has achieved explosive expansion in the cross-border market, becoming a landmark case in the global e-commerce sector. However, its rapid growth has also exposed deep-seated contradictions such as insufficient user loyalty, internal competition within the merchant ecosystem, narrowing profit margins, and intensified compliance risks. This paper takes Temu as a single case study object, based on platform economy theory and value symbiosis theory, to deconstruct the digital underlying logic of its cross-border expansion and reveal the formation mechanism of its digital paradox of “empowerment-constraint” duality. Furthermore, it constructs a strategic reconstruction path from “traffic harvesting” to “value symbiosis” from four dimensions: users, industry, region, and system. The research not only enriches the theoretical research on platform globalization but also provides an operable practical solution for Chinese cross-border e-commerce enterprises to go global with high quality.

title: Log-regularly varying scale mixture of asymmetric Laplaces for robust Bayesian quantile regression
summary: Bayesian quantile regression based on the asymmetric Laplace (AL) distribution can be sensitive to extreme observations because of its exponentially decaying tails. We propose a robust error distribution constructed as a finite mixture of t
content: Bayesian quantile regression based on the asymmetric Laplace (AL) distribution can be sensitive to extreme observations because of its exponentially decaying tails. We propose a robust error distribution constructed as a finite mixture of the AL distribution and a log-Pareto scale mixture of asymmetric Laplace distributions (LPAL). Unlike a direct log-Pareto extension of the normal location-scale representation of the AL distribution, the proposed AL-LPAL mixture preserves the prescribed quantile and exhibits log-regularly varying behavior in both tails. The LPAL component also has an unbounded density at the target quantile, yielding a distribution that combines sharp central concentration with super-heavy tails. We establish posterior robustness under arbitrarily extreme contamination and provide sufficient conditions for the existence of posterior moments of the regression coefficients and scale parameter. For posterior computation, we develop a Gibbs sampler using latent-variable augmentations and a computationally efficient mean-field variational Bayes approximation. Simulation studies show that the proposed method is competitive under moderate contamination and maintains stable point estimation with comparatively concentrated posterior intervals, particularly when severe contamination affects the quantile of interest. Applications to carbon dioxide and Boston housing data, using the same preprocessing as existing robust Bayesian quantile regression analyses, show favorable predictive performance across nearly all quantile levels and loss criteria considered.

title: REFLEXOS DOS EFEITOS CLIMÁTICOS NA SAÚDE: A INFLUÊNCIA DA EXPANSÃO URBANA E POLUIÇÃO DO AR
summary: As principais consequências dos efeitos climáticos e da poluição atmosférica para a saúde humana e a expansão da urbanização no Brasil, têm atraído a atenção dos estudos científicos acerca da sua interconexão. O desenho metodológico adotado
content: As principais consequências dos efeitos climáticos e da poluição atmosférica para a saúde humana e a expansão da urbanização no Brasil, têm atraído a atenção dos estudos científicos acerca da sua interconexão. O desenho metodológico adotado foi estruturado com base em uma pesquisa exploratória qualitativa, orientada pela revisão da literatura pertinente ao tema. O objetivo principal foi identificar os resultados dos recentes estudos de investigação sobre a correlação do crescimento urbano e poluição atmosférica, além da busca por respostas se há influências da poluição do ar nas doenças respiratórias. Especificamente, a busca na literatura de trabalhos sobre a poluição do ar em cidades brasileiras e os reflexos na saúde humana entre os anos de 2014 e 2023. Os 21 artigos analisados revelam as dificuldades na gestão brasileira das mudanças climáticas são intrinsecamente relacionados com a poluição do ar que corrobora para uma maior incidência de doenças respiratórias e cardiovasculares, pois o aumento das emissões de gases poluentes presentes nos veículos, assim como, o aumento da degradação ambiental e crescimento das indústrias regionais impactam na saúde populacional. Portanto, esses fatores climáticos, ações para reduções de emissões de gases e queimadas florestais que são nocivos à saúde humana e pioram a qualidade do ar deveriam ser melhor contemplados nas estruturas de governança, bem como, nas especificidades das políticas públicas regionais e nacional para que sejam implementadas de maneira eficiente e a maior punibilidade da legislação.

title: Environmental Groups Go It Alone in Oregon
summary: In late June 2019, Senate Democrats were all set to cast the decisive votes for historic legislation that would establish a cap-and-trade system and put Oregon on a path to a low-carbon economy.They waited for their colleagues to join them
content: In late June 2019, Senate Democrats were all set to cast the decisive votes for historic legislation that would establish a cap-and-trade system and put Oregon on a path to a low-carbon economy.They waited for their colleagues to join them on the floor, but the Republicans never arrived.Without twothirds of the chamber pre sent, the Senate could not cast a vote, stopping the climate bill in its tracks.Across the street, demonstrators with hardhats held up signs reading "Proud Oregon Logger" and "Long Live the Working Class," invoking latent fault lines from the Timber Wars ( Williams 2019).Governor Kate Brown eventually called on the state's police force to track down the missing Republican senators, prompting Senate minority leader Herman Baertschiger Jr. to respond from his Idaho hideout that "I don't think you're going to see us anytime soon" (Osborne and Youn 2019).The Republicans were still gone the following week, and the Democrats fi nally conceded that they no longer had the votes to pass the bill (Turkewitz 2019).Climate advocates were stunned by the Democrats' sudden reversal.The Renew Oregon co ali tion's executive director, Tera Hurst, emphasized that the Senate president had "promised a floor vote" and after the walkout had "gone back on his word."Spokesman Brad Reed added that "[as] far as we were concerned, we had the votes" and that the co ali tion "still believe [s] if it were taken to the floor it would have passed" (Radnovich and Loew 2019).The Republicans repeated the tactic the next year to block the bill a second time (Mena 2020).The contrast between Washington state and Oregon demonstrates how legislative gridlock incentivizes co ali tion building, while political opportunity-or, more precisely, the perception of such an opportunity-promotes a more autonomous approach to advocacy.In Washington state, the process 6 Environmental Groups Go It Alone in Oregon

title: A Coalition for a Just Transition in Colorado
summary: Like in Washington state, the climate legislation Colorado's governor, Jared Polis, signed into law in 2019 reflected years of work to bridge divides between labor and environmental advocates.The co ali tion began with a march through Denve
content: Like in Washington state, the climate legislation Colorado's governor, Jared Polis, signed into law in 2019 reflected years of work to bridge divides between labor and environmental advocates.The co ali tion began with a march through Denver, evolved into a facilitated dialogue, threatened to collapse during eleventh-hour legislative negotiations, and fi nally yielded a compromise that established the first government office in the nation devoted to ensuring a just energy transition.This outcome was all the more remarkable given Colorado communities' reliance on the coal and natu ral gas industries for employment and tax revenues, and it demonstrates labor's capacity to contribute to climate action even in carbon-intensive economies.Greater economic dependence on fossil fuels facilitates arguments against enacting climate policy.Given labor federations' core interest in creating and sustaining jobs, the notion that labor relies on fossil fuels and other carbon-intensive industries for employment decreases the likelihood that they will support stringent policies to reduce emissions.One environmental advocate in Colorado summed up the substantial challenge facing climate co ali tions in carbon-intensive states: Every thing about doing this is harder when you're coming from a fossil fuel producing state . . .The coal industry has less of a voice in Colorado now than they used to, but you know, the Colorado Mining Association used to be very formidable and they're still very active at the Capitol and they have a very strong political presence.The oil and gas industry spends flabbergasting, large amounts of money, time and energy touting the benefits of oil and gas production for the state.And it's all the messages that you would typically hear from the fossil fuel industry.You can't run your state without us; without us, your economy would collapse.We support all of these jobs.We support all of these indirect jobs, right?We are the reason why you have an economy.We are the reason why you have 7 A Co ali tion for a Just Transition in Colorado

title: Why Groups Build Coalitions
summary: Why do labor and environmental groups, or disparate movements more generally, build co ali tions?Prior research may help account for the rise and fall of labor-environmental co ali tions, as well as shed light on current and future opportun
content: Why do labor and environmental groups, or disparate movements more generally, build co ali tions?Prior research may help account for the rise and fall of labor-environmental co ali tions, as well as shed light on current and future opportunities.I therefore review the lit er a ture to identify the dominant explanations for these outcomes.These explanations leave open questions about when and why par tic u lar groups form co ali tions, as well as the process through which these co ali tions come together.I critique these explanations and state my own argument regarding the role political opportunity plays in spurring co ali tion formation.I also explain that organized labor's engagement in climate advocacy co ali tions represents a hard test of the theory, given historical tensions between the labor and environmental movements over environmental regulation.Labor leaders generally seek concessions that increase the certainty that climate policy proposals would provide jobs or at least mitigate the impact of job losses through targeted benefits.Legislative gridlock on climate policy increases environmentalists' incentive to make these concessions to labor in order to build a stronger co ali tion for current and future policy negotiations.This study seeks to identify the conditions under which interest groups join lobbying co ali tions.Much of the coalition-building lit er a ture focuses on protest co ali tions, which form to jointly mobilize participants for instances of collective action (see, e.g., Bearman and Everett 1993; Klatch 1999).While protest co ali tions contribute to social movement emergence (Van Dyke and McCammon 2010), they are not a sufficient condition for policy reform.Where the rubber meets the road-when a movement seeks to leverage its grassroots base to enact its favored policies-strategic movement actors must identify the allies whose support will persuade veto players within 3 Why Groups Build Co ali tions

title: Seaweed-Derived Feed Additives for Enteric Methane Mitigation in Cattle: Efficacy Evidence, Economic Incentives, and Policy Pathways for Smallholder and Commercial Dairy Systems
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The emissions from enteric methane by the world's 1.5 billion cattle is one of the largest and least tackled sources of agricultural GHGs. Livestock emissions are a critical factor in near term climate outcomes as methane has a global warmi
content: The emissions from enteric methane by the world's 1.5 billion cattle is one of the largest and least tackled sources of agricultural GHGs. Livestock emissions are a critical factor in near term climate outcomes as methane has a global warming potential of approximately 80 times more than carbon dioxide over a 20 year time horizon. This article explores an emerging mitigation pathway natural, seaweed based feed additives that inhibit the formation of CH4 in the rumen. It reviews peer-reviewed trials and meta analyses, dissects the biological mechanism of bromoform containing red seaweed to inhibit methanogenesis, and examines figures of actual reductions, which have been as high as 80% or more in some instances depending on the dose and conditions, as well as the economic case for adoption by smallholder farmers, dairy cooperatives, and corporate producers. The piece also places this technology in the context of changing regulations, such as the first ever livestock emissions tax in the world, which will come into effect in 2030, and the specific advantage for countries with a high number of cattle. Most importantly, it highlights unanswered questions regarding long term effectiveness, animal productivity, food safety and cost. The goal is to provide the public, policy makers and farming communities with fact based and balanced information on a technology that could be important for climate mitigation and for rural livelihoods as well.

title: CATASTROPHE BONDS AS AN INSTRUMENT FOR FINANCING CLIMATE RESILIENCE IN THE GLOBAL ECONOMY
summary: The purpose of the study is to assess the potential of catastrophe bonds (CAT Bonds) as an innovative tool for managing environmental and climate risks and integrating them into a sustainable financing system. The hypothesis of the study is
content: The purpose of the study is to assess the potential of catastrophe bonds (CAT Bonds) as an innovative tool for managing environmental and climate risks and integrating them into a sustainable financing system. The hypothesis of the study is that the use of catastrophic bonds contributes to the diversification of sources of financing for the consequences of emergencies by attracting private capital and redistributing risks between the insurance sector and the capital market. The scientific novelty of the work is to substantiate the role of catastrophic bonds as an element of the financial infrastructure of sustainable development, providing for the expansion of mechanisms to cover climate and natural risks in the context of the transformation of the global financial system. The methodological basis of the study was made up of comparative and institutional analysis, methods of systematic and comparative legal research, as well as an analysis of international experience in the use of CAT Bonds. The results obtained made it possible to determine the economic essence, functioning mechanism and advantages of catastrophic bonds, identify the features of their use in international practice and assess the prospects for the introduction of this instrument in the Russian Federation. The practical significance of the research results lies in the possibility of using the results obtained in the development of financing mechanisms for adaptation to climate change, improving tools for managing natural and climatic risks and forming a national market for sustainable finance. The prospects for further research are related to the development of models for issuing catastrophic bonds in Russian conditions, evaluating the effectiveness of their application and improving the regulatory support for the functioning of this financial instrument. Цель исследования заключается в оценке потенциала катастрофических облигаций (Catastrophe Bonds, CAT Bonds) как инновационного инструмента управления природно-климатическими рисками и их интеграции в систему устойчивого финансирования. Гипотеза исследования состоит в том, что использование катастрофических облигаций способствует диверсификации источников финансирования последствий чрезвычайных ситуаций за счет привлечения частного капитала и перераспределения рисков между страховым сектором и рынком капитала. title: Introducing a novel 28S rRNA marker for improved assessment of coral reef biodiversity
summary: Biodiversity monitoring based on DNA metabarcoding depends on primer performance. Here, we develop a new metabarcoding primer pair that targets a ~ 318 bp fragment of the 28S rRNA gene. We validate the primer pair in assessing sponges, a no
content: Biodiversity monitoring based on DNA metabarcoding depends on primer performance. Here, we develop a new metabarcoding primer pair that targets a ~ 318 bp fragment of the 28S rRNA gene. We validate the primer pair in assessing sponges, a notoriously challenging group for coral reef metabarcoding studies, by using mock and natural complex reef communities to examine its performance in species detection, amplification efficiency, and quantitative potential. Mock community experiments revealed a high number of sponge species (n = 94) spanning a broad taxonomic scope (15 orders), limited taxon-specific primer biases (only a single species exceeded a two-fold deviation from the expected number of reads), and its suitability for quantitative metabarcoding – there was a significant relationship between read abundance and visual percent coverage of sponge taxa (R = 0.76). In the natural complex coral reef community experiments, commonly used COI metabarcoding primers detected only 30.9% of sponge species, while the new 28S primer increased detection to 79.4%. These new 28S primers detect a broader taxonomic array of species across phyla and classes within the complex cryptobiome of coral reef communities than the Leray-Geller COI primers. As biodiversity assessments using metabarcoding tools are increasingly being leveraged for environmental monitoring and guide policymaking, these new 28S rRNA primers can improve biodiversity assessments for complex ecological coral reef communities.

title: A hybrid robust model to design a sustainable and resilient biofuel supply chain: A data-driven approach
summary: The increasing global demand for renewable energy and concerns over environmental issues and dependency on fossil fuels have increased the attention and need for efficient and sustainable biofuel supply chains. This study proposes a resilie
content: The increasing global demand for renewable energy and concerns over environmental issues and dependency on fossil fuels have increased the attention and need for efficient and sustainable biofuel supply chains. This study proposes a resilient and sustainable biofuel supply chain that minimizes operational costs while improving local employment opportunities. The problem is a bi-objective framework addressing location-allocation and transportation decisions, which integrates economic and social sustainability goals. To deal with uncertainties related to biomass availability, biofuel demand, price fluctuations, and facility disruptions, A hybrid robust optimization framework is employed, integrating scenario-based, polyhedral, and box uncertainty set approaches. Additionally, the self-organizing maps algorithm, a machine learning algorithm, is employed to cluster geographically dispersed suppliers, leading to efficiency in decision-making and model realism. The application of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a case study in Oregon, USA. In this case study, the designed model successfully provided the cost of biofuel production at $3.56 per gallon, created 809 jobs, and delivered the solutions with an objective function value that is 0.323% better compared to the robust-stochastic approach, which also showed higher stability when being disrupted. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is capable of balancing economic efficiency, resilience, and social sustainability. Furthermore, the proposed methodology will help to achieve Sustainable Development Goals 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure).

title: Can information transparency mitigate border pollution? Evidence from public data openness in China
summary: Pollution is often harder to control near administrative borders because pollution crosses jurisdictions while local governments regulate separately. This study examines whether public data openness (PDO) can reduce air pollution in such ar
content: Pollution is often harder to control near administrative borders because pollution crosses jurisdictions while local governments regulate separately. This study examines whether public data openness (PDO) can reduce air pollution in such areas. Using panel data for 281 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2011 to 2024, we exploit the staggered launch of municipal public data platforms and estimate a triple-difference model based on differences in cities’ border exposure. The results show that PDO reduces PM2.5 concentrations more strongly in cities with greater border exposure. At the sample mean of border exposure, the estimated reduction is approximately 5.38%, or 2.37 μ g / m 3 . Mechanism analyses using cross-provincial neighboring city pairs show that PDO is associated with more similar environmental priorities across neighboring governments, greater public attention to environmental issues on both sides of the border, and more joint green patents across neighboring cities. The pollution-reduction effect is stronger in larger cities, cities with better digital infrastructure, and cities closer to provincial capitals. We also find that higher-quality data openness produces larger environmental benefits. In addition, when neighboring cities also launch public data platforms, the pollution-reduction spillover effect becomes significantly stronger as border exposure increases. These findings suggest that PDO can complement conventional environmental regulation by making pollution conditions and regulatory actions easier to observe across administrative borders.

title: Ultramafic specialist lichens persist through flexible symbioses structured by climate-driven filtering and modulated by substrate effects
summary: Ultramafic substrates impose severe edaphic stress characterised by metal toxicity, nutrient imbalance, and extreme microclimatic conditions, creating spatially fragmented habitats that can shape evolutionary and ecological dynamics of asso
content: Ultramafic substrates impose severe edaphic stress characterised by metal toxicity, nutrient imbalance, and extreme microclimatic conditions, creating spatially fragmented habitats that can shape evolutionary and ecological dynamics of associated organisms. Together with climatic variation, such factors may also influence the structure of holobiont communities of lichenized fungi. Here we investigated the ultramafic specialist lichen Solenopsora liparina across its entire range. We contextualized its symbiotic associations using calcicolous congeners ( S. candicans and S. cesatii ), as ecological reference taxa representing contrasting substrate-associated lineages within the sampled dataset, to assess how climatic filtering acting within a specialised edaphic niche structures symbiotic partner diversity and composition. Photobionts and endolichenic fungi displayed climate-associated compositional turnover and lineage-level diversity. Variation in the composition of these symbionts was most strongly associated with precipitation during the warmest quarter and, in photobionts, with altitude and temperature seasonality. In photobionts, dominant lineages differed in their relative occurrence among host taxa, whereas low-abundance lineages were broadly shared across samples within the dataset. Despite this turnover, alpha diversity remained generally stable across environmental gradients, indicating that climatic variation most strongly affects community composition rather than within-sample diversity. The results are consistent with a model of mixed host- and substrate- associated symbiont assembly, in which dominant photobiont lineages exhibit host- or substrate-linked preferences, whereas low-abundance associates show weaker specificity and broader ecological overlap across environmental and host contexts. Overall, the findings indicate that climatic factors structure the composition of symbiotic partners without strongly altering their overall diversity, while variation among host taxa is reflected in lineage turnover of dominant symbionts. The persistence of the ultramafic specialist lichen S. liparina thus appears to rely on flexible, compositionally dynamic symbiotic associations shaped by climatic variation within a spatially and edaphically constrained niche, rather than obligate partner specificity. Substrate effects are interpreted here as host-associated lineage patterns rather than independently quantified drivers. More broadly, the results suggest that climatic variation can in some cases strongly influence symbiotic assembly within environmentally extreme and spatially heterogeneous systems. Substrate specialisation provides the ecological context in which such interactions occur. Together, the findings highlight the importance of climatic variation in shaping symbiotic assembly within an edaphically specialised system, emphasizing that patterns associated with host and substrate context are expressed mainly through lineage turnover ra

title: Green Banking: A Systematic Literature Review of Developed and Developing Countries
summary: ABSTRACT Green banks attract private investment to green projects, facilitating affordable transitions to climate‐resilient economies. However, the existing literature remains fragmented, lacking cross‐country analyses connecting theory, po
content: ABSTRACT Green banks attract private investment to green projects, facilitating affordable transitions to climate‐resilient economies. However, the existing literature remains fragmented, lacking cross‐country analyses connecting theory, policy design and institutional practice within a multi‐framework, especially regarding the roles of central banks, financial regulators and financial institutions. This paper addresses this gap through a systematic literature review of green banking in both developed and developing countries, with a focus on regulatory tools and financial instruments. The findings identify key trends, recurring definitional patterns and comparative typologies of green banking models and regulatory frameworks. The review indicates that developed countries rely on market‐based and risk‐oriented tools, whereas developing countries adopt more directive and allocative approaches. The review's novelty lies in integrating a macro‐meso‐micro logic into institutional maturity, policy mechanisms and outcomes perspective. This integrated framework (MMM‐IPMO) provides a vertical multi‐level structure and horizontal causal mechanism to examine how central banks, financial regulators and financial institutions interact to translate institutional maturity and policy mechanisms into outcomes, offering a structured foundation for future theoretical and empirical research.

title: Carbon Lock-in Challenges and Unlocking Pathways for Resource-Based Cities in Sichuan Province under the "Dual-Carbon" Goals
source: Journal of Mathematical Finance and Risk Management
summary: Based on carbon lock-in theory, this paper examines the manifestations, causes, and unlocking pathways of carbon lock-in in resource-based cities in Sichuan Province from three aspects: energy structure adjustment, institutional development
content: Based on carbon lock-in theory, this paper examines the manifestations, causes, and unlocking pathways of carbon lock-in in resource-based cities in Sichuan Province from three aspects: energy structure adjustment, institutional development, and changes in social behavior. The results show that carbon lock-in in these cities is mainly reflected in the strong inertia of traditional fossil fuel consumption, pronounced path dependence on resource-based industries, and clear regional differences. Energy, institutional, and social lock-in interact and reinforce one another, making low-carbon transition more difficult. Therefore, city-specific and differentiated policies should be adopted from three aspects—optimizing the energy supply structure, improving relevant policy measures, and strengthening social coordination—to break carbon lock-in constraints and promote the sustainable development and high-quality transition of resource-based cities in Sichuan Province.

title: Efficiency of Manufacturing Firms Practicing ESG: Comparative Study from Selected Advanced and Emerging Asia Pacific Countries
source: International Journal of Economics and Management
summary: The growing attention to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices has shifted business horizons, focusing on both financial metrics and sustainable operations to remain competitive and sustainable. However, the existing literat
content: The growing attention to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices has shifted business horizons, focusing on both financial metrics and sustainable operations to remain competitive and sustainable. However, the existing literature remains largely focused on financial institutions. To some extent, it narrowly concentrates on the context of a single country, overlooking the significance of maintaining efficiency for firms that are highly dependent on the effective management of resources. Correspondingly, the study examines the operational efficiency level, particularly in terms of profit, revenue and cost efficiency, of manufacturing firms practicing ESG in two selected categories of Asia Pacific (APAC) countries: advanced and emerging. This study employed Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to examine the efficiency levels of 452 manufacturing firms, comprising 300 firms from advanced and 152 firms from emerging countries. Accordingly, the results reveal remarkable findings that manufacturing firms practicing ESG in selected advanced APAC countries are less efficient than those in emerging countries. In particular, these firms exhibit lower efficiency levels, including revenue, cost, and subsequent profit efficiency. The difference in means for the efficiency level is consistently significant at the 1 percent level when assessed with a parametric t-test and robust non-parametric Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon Rank-sum) and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Overall, the results offer valuable insights for firms on how to efficiently manage their resources to maximize profits.

title: Accelerating the Adoption of Residential Solar Power Systems: Policy Analysis using a Dynamic Structural Model
summary: Problem definition: Solar electricity generation is a strategic component of energy portfolios designed to meet growing demand and reduce carbon emissions. Governments and municipalities encourage household photovoltaic (PV) adoption throug
content: Problem definition: Solar electricity generation is a strategic component of energy portfolios designed to meet growing demand and reduce carbon emissions. Governments and municipalities encourage household photovoltaic (PV) adoption through upfront rebates and tax credits. Limited budgets require principled, data-driven policies that account for the drivers of adoption and the effects of incentives on adoption rates. Methodology/results: We develop a dynamic structural model of residential PV diffusion based on adoption decisions by forward-looking households that weigh the economic trade-offs between installing now and later. Adoption depends on return on investment and influence from neighboring adopters. The model segments households by home value and urbanization level, incorporates unobserved heterogeneity, and captures spatiotemporal installation dynamics. We estimate the model using Bayesian methods and detailed household-level data from Austin, Texas. In out-of-sample tests, it predicts installations more accurately than contemporary alternatives. We simulate counterfactual policies within the dynamic equilibrium of PV diffusion to evaluate rebate designs. The framework can also be adapted to study the adoption of other durable technologies. Managerial implications: A rebate offered for a limited period generates more adoption and emissions reductions than a prolonged, costlier program. This counterintuitive result arises from forward-looking behavior, neighbor influence, and accelerated adoption before the rebate expires. We also evaluate phased reductions and rebates differentiated by household segment. A two-step reduction outperforms multiple small reductions. Geographic differentiation improves policy performance, whereas differentiation by home value offers little advantage over a uniform rebate.

title: Balancing Economic Growth and Environmental Harm: finding the Best mix
summary: The significance of this research lies in balancing economic expansion with environmental protection. The subject concerns the relationship between GDP growth from manufacturing investment and environmental harm. The research aims to establ
content: The significance of this research lies in balancing economic expansion with environmental protection. The subject concerns the relationship between GDP growth from manufacturing investment and environmental harm. The research aims to establish a framework for selecting the preferred investment option among manufacturing industry choices, based on the “increase in environmental damage / increase in GDP” ratio. The authors implemented a method that completely considers the effect of investments on economic dynamics and the resulting environmental harm, including both direct and indirect effects of investments. Consequently , mathematical models were created to facilitate this goal. The authors concluded that when the optimal investment allocation model in terms of the “increase in environmental damage / increase in GDP” ratio cannot be achieved because of resource limitations and all other feasible options must be employed.

title: Petroleum and the Green Gospel: Religious Pathways to Energy Transition and Environmental Remediation in the Niger Delta
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This research studies the environmental politics and remediation in a setting historically impacted by pollution due to oil and gas. This study has two objectives; first, to investigate the influence of religious institutions on environment
content: This research studies the environmental politics and remediation in a setting historically impacted by pollution due to oil and gas. This study has two objectives; first, to investigate the influence of religious institutions on environmental behaviour, remediation governance and community trust and second, to assess how faith-based ethical frameworks could enhance the social acceptance of emerging clean-energy technologies and low-carbon transition pathways. Using a combination of different research methods – that is, systematic literature review, documentary analysis, and thematic synthesis – the paper assesses the religious narratives and institutional responses and community-based ecological ethics that drive decarburization discourses and remediation outcomes. Faith institutions can offer a moral anchor for environmental action, help mobilize people on the ground, and make remediation efforts more credible, research finds. This reinforces public knowledge of hydrogen, carbon capture and storage, Nano bioremediation, and gas-based transition fuels, which ultimately removes public distrust of state environmental measures. The research concludes that the obstacles to environmental remediation and energy transition in the Niger Delta are not merely technical or regulatory but are fundamentally embedded in social trust, moral leadership and community engagement. According to its recommendation, a coordinated Faith-Remediation-Transition (FRT) model should be operationalized. There must be strengthened partnerships between environmental institutions and religious bodies. Meanwhile, local governance systems must be integrated with climate ethics. Finally, there must be alignment of faith-driven EE with national clean-energy transition strategy. This will aid a just, credible and community-owned sustainable future.

title: Post-Pandemic Adaptive Reuse: Transforming Underutilized Commercial Buildings into Affordable Housing in Ibadan, Nigeria: Office-to-Housing Conversion in Nigeria
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated structural changes in workplace organization, resulting in sustained vacancy in commercial buildings across many urban centres. At the same time, Nigerian cities continue to experience severe housing defici
content: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated structural changes in workplace organization, resulting in sustained vacancy in commercial buildings across many urban centres. At the same time, Nigerian cities continue to experience severe housing deficits, particularly for low- and lower-middle-income households. This coexistence of underutilized commercial space and unmet residential demand presents a critical urban planning challenge. Despite growing international interest in office-to-residential conversion, limited research has examined the feasibility of such adaptive reuse strategies within rapidly urbanizing African contexts characterized by infrastructural instability, regulatory rigidity, and constrained development finance. This study evaluates the architectural feasibility, economic viability, regulatory constraints, and affordability implications of converting commercial buildings into residential housing in Lagos, Abuja, and Ibadan. Using a mixed-methods approach that integrates survey data, comparative case analysis, and policy evaluation, the research examines building adaptability, service retrofitting requirements, zoning limitations, and financing barriers. Findings indicate that while many reinforced concrete office buildings possess structural capacity for conversion, high retrofitting costs, approval delays, and limited incentive frameworks significantly restrict scalability. Furthermore, market-driven conversion alone is unlikely to deliver affordable housing without targeted public-sector intervention. By engaging with this case, readers will be able to assess the practical viability of commercial-to-residential adaptive reuse in Nigerian cities and evaluate the policy reforms necessary to align post-pandemic vacancy with inclusive housing delivery.

title: Green Accounting and Economic Sustainability of listed Oil and Gas Firms in Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: This study evaluated the effect of green accounting on economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. Specifically, the study examined the effect environmental pollution prevention disclosure, waste management disclosure an
content: This study evaluated the effect of green accounting on economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. Specifically, the study examined the effect environmental pollution prevention disclosure, waste management disclosure and carbon emission on the economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. The study deployed ex-post facto research design. Eight listed oil and gas firms made up the population of the study while the sample size was six oil and gas firms. Secondary data were gleaned from the annual reports of the firms for a period of twelve years (2013 – 2024). The data were descriptive analysed. Robust least square regression was used in estimating the multiple regression coefficients and p-values for hypotheses testing. The results revealed that: environmental pollution prevention disclosure significantly and positively affects economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria (b = 0.0969, p-value = 0.0000); waste management disclosure has a significant but negative effect on economic sustainability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria (b = -0.0273, p-value = 0.0000); Carbon emission disclosure has a significant but negative effect on financial stability of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria (b -0.0276, p-value = 0.0000); In conclusion, green accounting enhances the financial standing of listed oil and gas firms except in cases where the cost associated with green accounting practices outweigh the benefits. The study recommends that oil and gas firms in Nigeria should conduct a thorough audit of their waste management practices, focusing on identifying inefficiencies and adopting circular economy principles where possible; this information should be disclosed annually in their sustainability reports, supported by independent verification, to mitigate any potential negative financial impacts and demonstrate responsible corporate governance. title: Green Economy Transitions in Kolkata through the Adoption of Electric Mobility
summary: Transportation is one of the most energy-intensive and greenhouse gas (GHG)–emitting sectors in developing country cities, where diesel-powered buses dominate public transit. Transitioning to cleaner technologies is urgent to meet climate g
content: Transportation is one of the most energy-intensive and greenhouse gas (GHG)–emitting sectors in developing country cities, where diesel-powered buses dominate public transit. Transitioning to cleaner technologies is urgent to meet climate goals and improve urban air quality. Electric mobility, particularly electric buses (e-buses), offers a promising low-carbon alternative. While cities in China and Europe have made significant strides in bus electrification, Indian cities are at a nascent stage. Kolkata was amongst the pioneers, launching one of India&s;s earliest large-scale e-bus pilot projects by deploying 80 e-buses between 2017 and 2020. This chapter examines Kolkata&s;s transition towards a green economy through its adoption of electric mobility, highlighting the policy frameworks, institutional arrangements, and operational experiences that shaped this transition. It also assesses the potential for large-scale uptake, explores challenges in scaling, and identifies opportunities for creating green jobs, especially in vehicle maintenance, charging infrastructure, and battery lifecycle management in a just transition framework

title: Dual Subsidy Policies and Pricing Decisions of Cross-Border E-commerce Supply Chain
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: There is synergy space for dual subsidy policies, but precise threshold management is required to improve the comprehensive benefits of the entire supply chain. Both government promotion subsidies and platform tariff subsidies are regarded
content: There is synergy space for dual subsidy policies, but precise threshold management is required to improve the comprehensive benefits of the entire supply chain. Both government promotion subsidies and platform tariff subsidies are regarded as key means to promote the development of cross-border e-commerce supply chains, yet the synergy mechanism of the two subsidies remains unclear. Against the background of intensifying tariff trade frictions, this paper constructs a game model with the participation of the government, cross-border e-commerce platforms, settled merchants and overseas consumers, and compares and analyzes supply chain pricing decisions under four scenarios: no subsidy, platform tariff subsidy only, government subsidy only, and coexistence of dual subsidies. The results show that a single subsidy policy cannot fully offset the negative impact of rising tariffs. Meanwhile, excessive platform subsidies will squeeze their promotion budgets and may induce merchants to raise prices. Although the linkage of dual subsidies can slow down the decline of demand under high tariff conditions, its effect is restricted by multiple factors such as subsidy intensity and tariff level.

title: Role Of Digital Accounting Transformation And Supply Chain Integration In Enhancing Financial Market Participation And Entrepreneurial Sustainability
source: International Journal of Computer Information Systems and Industrial Management Applications
summary: Digital accounting and digitally integrated supply chains are often treated as separate operational projects, yet both determine whether small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can produce credible information, demonstrate execution capac
content: Digital accounting and digitally integrated supply chains are often treated as separate operational projects, yet both determine whether small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can produce credible information, demonstrate execution capacity, and engage repeatedly with formal financial markets. This study develops an integrative capability framework explaining how digital accounting transformation and supply chain integration jointly enhance financial market participation and entrepreneurial sustainability. A transparent integrative literature review was conducted using 30 peer-reviewed and authoritative institutional sources published between 1991 and June 2026. The corpus was coded for focal construct, mechanism, financing outcome, sustainability outcome, and boundary condition. The synthesis shows that digital accounting primarily improves timeliness, comparability, traceability, and verifiability of financial information, while supply chain integration converts information quality into operational evidence through coordinated procurement, inventory, sales, receivables, and partner relationships. Their complementarity reduces information asymmetry and transaction costs, strengthens forecasting and cash-flow credibility, and improves readiness for bank credit, trade and asset-based finance, fintech assessment, equity, and sustainable finance. Financial market participation then supports resilience, innovation, responsible growth, and environmental and social value creation; however, the pathway is weakened by poor data governance, capability gaps, cybersecurity exposure, incompatible systems, algorithmic bias, and power asymmetry with dominant partners. Six theory-grounded propositions and a five-stage implementation pathway are proposed. The paper contributes by repositioning accounting systems and supply-chain integration as mutually reinforcing market-participation capabilities rather than isolated efficiency tools. It also offers an auditable research agenda for longitudinal, multi-country testing.

title: Pengaruh Capital Expenditure, Persistensi Laba dan Cash Holding Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
source: JAMPARING Jurnal Akuntansi Manajemen Pariwisata dan Pembelajaran Konseling
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh capital expenditure, persistensi laba dan cash holding terhadap nilai perusahaan pada perusahaan sektor industri yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) periode tahun 2020-2024. Jenis
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh capital expenditure, persistensi laba dan cash holding terhadap nilai perusahaan pada perusahaan sektor industri yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) periode tahun 2020-2024. Jenis penelitian ini yaitu pendekatan kuantitatif dengan menggunakan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan perusahaan melalui www.idx.co.id. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan purposive sampling sesuai dengan kriteria yang telah ditentukan. Data yang digunakan berupa data panel yang setelah proses pengolahan data dan penghapusan data outlier diperoleh total sampel sebanyak 165 perusahaan. Analisis data yang digunakan yaitu analisis regresi data panel dengan menggunakan alat bantu E-views 12. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa capital expenditure berpengaruh terhadap nilai perusahaan, namun persistensi laba dan cash holding tidak berpengaruh terhadap nilai perusahaan. Hasil penelitian ini juga menunjukkan bahwa capital expenditure, persistensi laba dan cash holding secara bersama-sama berpengaruh terhadap nilai perusahaan.

title: ESG fund flows under shocks: Are they more resilient against macro-financial shocks?
summary: This study examines whether environmental, social and governance (ESG) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) provide greater stability than conventional ETFs during periods of macro-financial stress. Using global equity ETF data from January 2015 to
content: This study examines whether environmental, social and governance (ESG) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) provide greater stability than conventional ETFs during periods of macro-financial stress. Using global equity ETF data from January 2015 to June 2023, we employ fixed-effects ordinary least squares (OLS) regression models to analyse fund flow responses to three distinct types of shocks: heightened market stress, elevated economic policy uncertainty, and tightening global monetary conditions. Our findings reveal that ESG ETFs experience significantly smaller outflows than their non-ESG counterparts across all shock scenarios. This effect is heterogeneous: it is more pronounced for ETFs domiciled in emerging markets during market stress, and stronger for ETFs with greater investment exposure to emerging market economies (EMEs) when policy uncertainty rises. These results suggest that the development of ESG fund markets may enhance financial stability by contributing to more resilient capital flow dynamics. Consequently, we argue for targeted policy measures to promote the development of the ESG fund market.

title: Forecast-driven optimal sizing and management of hybrid battery–hydrogen energy storage systems for renewable microgrids using a hybrid metaheuristic optimization
summary: Accurate short-term load forecasting can substantially improve the sizing and supervisory energy management of hybrid battery-hydrogen storage systems in renewable microgrids. This study proposes a forecast-informed optimization framework t
content: Accurate short-term load forecasting can substantially improve the sizing and supervisory energy management of hybrid battery-hydrogen storage systems in renewable microgrids. This study proposes a forecast-informed optimization framework that integrates one-hour-ahead Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) forecasting with a hybrid Improved Harmony Search–Simulated Annealing optimization algorithm for the optimal sizing and hourly supervisory scheduling of an off-grid photovoltaic-wind-battery-hydrogen-diesel microgrid. The framework is evaluated using one year of hourly measured load and meteorological data and five forecasting feature sets. Across five independent LSTM runs per feature set, the LOAD + ALL configuration provides the highest forecasting accuracy and the most stable predictive performance. The proposed algorithm is compared with Harmony Search, Simulated Annealing, and Particle Swarm Optimization using 40 independent optimization runs under a reliability constraint. Results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently achieves the lowest mean Total Net Annual Cost while maintaining competitive computational performance and greater robustness than the benchmark algorithms. Additional sensitivity analyses over reliability targets and diesel fuel prices reveal important trade-offs among economic cost, reliability, renewable fraction, and lifecycle CO 2 emissions. The results demonstrate that integrating accurate short-term forecasting with hybrid metaheuristic optimization provides an effective and practical framework for the optimal sizing and supervisory energy management of renewable microgrids.

title: Culture, Politics, Identity, and the Rival Kingdoms of the Heart
summary: Politics can become a form of false assurance when legitimate concern for justice, life, family, freedom, security, poverty, corruption, religious liberty, racial reconciliation, environmental stewardship, or human dignity hardens into savi
content: Politics can become a form of false assurance when legitimate concern for justice, life, family, freedom, security, poverty, corruption, religious liberty, racial reconciliation, environmental stewardship, or human dignity hardens into saving trust in a party, nation, ideology, leader, grievance, or vision of world order. This chapter argues that the New Testament neither commands political withdrawal nor authorizes political idolatry. Civil authority is real but limited under God; Christians may vote, serve, govern, advocate, protest lawfully, pursue reform, and defend the vulnerable, but no state, movement, leader, or international system can regenerate sinners or establish the kingdom Jesus Christ will consummate.The chapter examines partisan captivity, nationalism and Christian nationalism, state worship and political messianism, ideological idolatry on the left and right, tribal and racial loyalties, patriotism, conspiracy and fear, propaganda, activism that displaces evangelism, environmental stewardship and spiritualized nature, identity politics and victimhood, competing nationalist and globalist utopias, justice without gospel, dehumanization of political opponents, and the kingdom of God as the final horizon of Christian public faithfulness. It distinguishes patriotism from nationalism, political participation from partisan captivity, international cooperation from supranational absolutism, structural justice from group-based salvation, and evidence-based investigation from rumor or unfalsifiable conspiracy.The chapter also confronts New Age and quasi-religious alternatives in which nature, planetary consciousness, manifestation, evolutionary awakening, or sacralized humanity is offered as collective redemption. Against both progressive and conservative political religion, Scripture insists on the Creator-creature distinction, Christ's exclusive saving lordship, the dignity of every image-bearer, truthful witness, limited government, justice, enemy love, and the church's transnational identity in the Lamb. The pastoral summons is not political apathy and not political capture, but public faithfulness under Christ. No flag is a cross, no party is a church, no grievance is a gospel, and no earthly victory is a ground of assurance. The believer's citizenship is in heaven and public discipleship must therefore be marked by truth, courage, humility, repentance, neighbor love, holiness, and readiness for the returning King.

title: The Role of Transport Infrastructure in Regional Economic Development
summary: Transport infrastructure is one of the most important factors influencing regional economic development, economic integration, and long-term competitiveness. Efficient transportation systems improve connectivity between urban and rural area
content: Transport infrastructure is one of the most important factors influencing regional economic development, economic integration, and long-term competitiveness. Efficient transportation systems improve connectivity between urban and rural areas, facilitate trade activities, and increase the mobility of labor, goods, and services. Modern infrastructure networks, including highways, railways, airports, and ports, play a significant role in reducing transportation costs, improving logistics performance, and enhancing market accessibility. Regions with developed transportation systems are generally more attractive for domestic and foreign investment because they provide greater operational efficiency and support industrial and commercial expansion. This article examines the relationship between transport infrastructure and regional economic growth from economic, social, and technological perspectives. The study analyzes how transportation systems contribute to productivity growth, employment generation, regional integration, and business development. In addition to economic benefits, transport infrastructure also improves access to education, healthcare, and public services, thereby increasing social welfare and reducing regional inequalities. The article further explores the impact of modern technologies such as Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS), Big Data analytics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT) on transportation management and operational efficiency. The research also discusses major challenges related to transport infrastructure development, including high investment costs, environmental issues, traffic congestion, and unequal regional investment distribution. The findings emphasize that sustainable and smart transportation systems are essential for achieving balanced regional development, environmental sustainability, and long-term economic stability in the modern global economy

title: How to Blow Up an AI Data Center
summary: This essay advocates a critical pedagogical orientation to AI guided by a politics of refusal. I pursue this advocacy by, first, showing how the social and environmental harms of AI technology outweigh any promises to its social good and th
content: This essay advocates a critical pedagogical orientation to AI guided by a politics of refusal. I pursue this advocacy by, first, showing how the social and environmental harms of AI technology outweigh any promises to its social good and then, second, locating resonances between our contemporary technological situation and similar inflection points in the histories of labor organizing and environmental justice activism. Together, these material implications of the emergent technology help form a pedagogical framework for how communication educators can advance critical literacy about AI in the classroom as a constructive counterpoint to its uncritical adoption in the learning process. The title of the essay takes overt inspiration from Andreas Malm’s (2021) environmental activist manifesto How to Blow Up a Pipeline, a text advocating direct action in the form of literal destruction of climate change’s greatest infrastructural contributors. While my essay neither explicitly advocates property destruction nor pedagogical approaches that direct students toward specific forms of political action, its ethos is in keeping with Malm when he writes: “Recognising the directness of the situation, it is high time for the movement to more decisively shift from protest to resistance” (2021, p. 70).

title: A Simple and Adaptive Confidence Interval when Nuisance Parameters Satisfy an Inequality
source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Inequalities may appear in many models. They can be as simple as assuming a parameter is nonnegative, possibly a regression coefficient or a treatment effect. This paper focuses on models with one inequality and proposes an inequality-impos
content: Inequalities may appear in many models. They can be as simple as assuming a parameter is nonnegative, possibly a regression coefficient or a treatment effect. This paper focuses on models with one inequality and proposes an inequality-imposed confidence interval (IICI) that has particularly attractive features. The IICI is simple in that it does not require simulations or tuning parameters. Also, the IICI is adaptive to the slackness of the inequality, uniformly valid, and never longer than the usual confidence interval. We demonstrate the IICI in two empirical applications. The first empirical application considers a regression when a coefficient is known to be nonpositive. The second empirical application considers an instrumental variables regression when the endogeneity of a regressor is known to be nonnegative.

title: Service Life Distribution of Timber Buildings in South Korea Based on National Demolition Big Data
summary: Building service life is a critical parameter in lifecycle assessment; however, current assessments often rely on arbitrary standards. This study analyzed the empirical service life of buildings using South Korean national building-register
content: Building service life is a critical parameter in lifecycle assessment; however, current assessments often rely on arbitrary standards. This study analyzed the empirical service life of buildings using South Korean national building-register data, categorizing 1,419,867 records into timber, masonry, steel, and concrete structures. Service life distributions were evaluated according to regional, structural, and functional factors. The results showed that while region and building scale had minimal impact, building use significantly influenced the service life of timber, masonry, and steel. Survival analysis using Weibull and Gamma distributions estimated the empirical service life to be 58.1 years for timber, 30.8 years for masonry, 22.1 years for concrete, and 10.6 years for steel. The notably shorter service life of concrete and steel compared with timber illustrates a “demolition inversion phenomenon,” where socioeconomic factors—such as urban redevelopment—drive building demolition regardless of structural durability. While results for steel and concrete reflect current replacement cycles, the 58.1-year service life of timber aligns with international benchmarks for carbon storage. These findings highlight the urgent need to revise the current 20-year legal standard for timber structures to more accurately reflect their long-term carbon sequestration potential and promote sustainable wooden architecture in carbon-neutrality policies.

title: Technical and Engineering Challenges in Scaling Up Microwave-Assisted Pyrolysis of Waste Plastics
summary: Microwave‑assisted pyrolysis (MAP) has emerged as a promising thermochemical route for converting waste plastics into fuels, chemicals, and carbon materials, offering fast volumetric heating, lower apparent reaction temperatures, and distin
content: Microwave‑assisted pyrolysis (MAP) has emerged as a promising thermochemical route for converting waste plastics into fuels, chemicals, and carbon materials, offering fast volumetric heating, lower apparent reaction temperatures, and distinctive product selectivity compared with conventional pyrolysis. At present, however, MAP of plastics is still largely confined to laboratory and bench‑scale batch reactors, corresponding mainly to laboratory and pilot technology readiness levels, and the engineering barriers to continuous, large‑scale operation remain poorly understood. This review critically examines the technical and engineering challenges that hinder the scale‑up of MAP for plastic waste valorisation, complementing existing chemistry‑focused reviews that emphasize process parameters and product yields. The key scale‑up barriers discussed include: (i) electromagnetic field non‑uniformity and limited microwave penetration depth in larger cavities, leading to hot spots, thermal runaway, and variable product quality; (ii) design and operation of continuous feeding systems for thermoplastic melts and mixed solid feeds, including mechanical integration of screw feeders, conveyors, and augers in high‑temperature microwave environments; (iii) susceptor selection, durability, and in‑process management (SiC, activated carbon, in‑situ char); (iv) real‑time temperature measurement and process control under microwave irradiation; (v) feedstock variability and the heterogeneous dielectric behaviour of post‑consumer plastic streams; (vi) downstream product quality requirements and constraints for refinery and steam‑cracker integration; and (vii) the current status of coupled multiphysics modelling (electromagnetic–thermal–CFD–reaction) and emerging digital‑twin approaches for reactor and process scale‑up. Reported techno‑economic analyses and life‑cycle assessments suggest that MAP can reduce energy use and greenhouse‑gas emissions relative to conventional plastic pyrolysis under favorable conditions, but robust pilot‑scale datasets and validated process models remain limited. By systematically mapping these unresolved engineering challenges onto recent advances in reactor design, susceptor engineering, process monitoring, Multiphysics simulation, and industrial pilot lines, this review proposes a lab‑to‑pilot‑to‑industrial roadmap for plastic MAP. It identifies priority research directions to advance MAP toward commercial deployment and clarifies its potential role within a broader circular economy framework for plastic waste.

title: Biofuel Production from Microalgae: A Critical Update on Cultivation, Conversion, System Integration and Commercial Readiness
summary: Microalgae remain scientifically compelling biofuel feedstocks because they can convert light and carbon into chemically diverse biomass without an intrinsic requirement for fertile agricultural land, while some production systems can also
content: Microalgae remain scientifically compelling biofuel feedstocks because they can convert light and carbon into chemically diverse biomass without an intrinsic requirement for fertile agricultural land, while some production systems can also use saline water, wastewater nutrients and concentrated carbon dioxide streams. Yet the field has not translated laboratory demonstrations into routine production of competitively priced, low-carbon commodity fuels. This critical narrative review evaluates why that gap persists and how the research agenda has changed. Literature published from 1 January 2015 to 22 June 2026 was examined, with earlier seminal studies retained where necessary to establish mechanisms, process benchmarks and the evolution of sustainability arguments. Evidence was synthesised across strain physiology and engineering, cultivation, harvesting and dewatering, lipid-based biodiesel, hydrothermal liquefaction, pyrolysis, anaerobic digestion, carbohydrate-derived fuels, wastewater and carbon integration, techno-economics and life-cycle assessment. The central finding is that microalgal fuel performance is governed by cross-stage interactions rather than by a single favourable trait such as lipid content. Stress-induced lipid accumulation can reduce biomass productivity; controlled photobioreactors can improve culture performance while increasing capital and energy burdens; and downstream choices determine whether dilute wet biomass becomes an energetic liability or a useful feedstock. Hydrothermal liquefaction is particularly compatible with wet whole biomass, whereas conventional biodiesel benefits from mature chemistry but is constrained by selective lipid recovery and drying or extraction requirements. Wastewater, nutrient recycling, carbon utilisation and coproduct valorisation can improve system performance, but benefits are strongly context dependent and may be overstated when environmental-service credits or high-value coproduct revenues are assumed without scale-consistent markets. Pilot-informed life-cycle studies continue to show substantial sensitivity to electricity supply, infrastructure, productivity, nutrient source, dewatering and allocation choices. The most defensible near-term direction is therefore not a universal algal-fuel process, but location-specific, integrated biorefineries in which fuel production is co-designed with nutrient recovery, carbon management and realistic coproduct pathways. Progress towards commercial relevance requires continuous outdoor validation, harmonised assessment, wet-processing strategies and evidence that integrated gains persist at scale.

title: Editorial: Global conservation of vulnerable, threatened and endangered seagrass
summary: Seagrasses are flowering marine plants that evolved from terrestrial ancestors about 100 million years ago. They spread to cover many shallow marine systems on all continents of the world, except Antarctica. Though seagrasses are simultaneo
content: Seagrasses are flowering marine plants that evolved from terrestrial ancestors about 100 million years ago. They spread to cover many shallow marine systems on all continents of the world, except Antarctica. Though seagrasses are simultaneously recognized as a model marine vegetation community and critical coastal marine and fisheries habitat, many vulnerable, threatened, and endangered seagrass species and subpopulations remain a black box when it comes to our understanding of basic taxonomy, biology, and biogeographical trends. Increasing global and climate changes are known to alter and destroy seagrass meadows significantly. Many researchers fear this is having a catastrophic impact on global seagrass conservation. Advancement in international collaborations, technological research and development and growth of socio-cultural networks are rapidly improving global reconnaissance and capabilities for recovery following loss. There is an urgent need to collate and highlight research, reviews, policy, and opinions aimed at advancing global seagrass species survival.Seagrasses are represented by a relatively small number of species but are characterised by extensive seabed coverage and significance in coastal ecosystems as habitat builders, providing a broad range of ecosystem services, such as food supply, stabilisation of coastlines and carbon sequestration (Duarte et al., 2025). While some seagrass beds are largely found growing in monoculture (for instance Zostera marina in the temperate north Pacific and Atlantic, and many regions have a common suite of widely distributed species(for example the tropical Indo-Pacific region), endemism is also common in some regions, e.g., Verduin and Waycott (2026). There are also some species with limited distribution, leading to concerns about genetic diversity and species-level conservation. This is of particular concern as ecosystems restoration programs proliferate around the world.Problems are compounded by lack of awareness and expertise to monitor seagrasses. Many seagrass populations have been inadequately documented and surveyed, which is often difficult due to turbidity, although advances in technology, especially remote sensing and global databases, including citizen science sources, have improved this situation in recent years, e.g., Trinh et al. (2023); Giménez-Romero et al. (2024); Konzewitsch and Evans (2024); Jones et al. (2025). Effective conservation is further compromised by the proximity of many seagrass meadows to shorelines, where they are vulnerable to human activities, especially in highly developed regions. A global increase in awareness of the ecological services provided by seagrass ecosystems has improved scientific effort in seagrass monitoring and science, leading to improved input into conservation policy and management, however, there are still many gaps in the records of seagrass distribution, abundance and condition, e.g., Zakaria et al. (2025b), leading to imperfect assessm

title: Sustainable cork-based laser-induced graphene sensors for humidity monitoring in cultural heritage preservation
summary: Sustainable sensing platforms are essential for environmental monitoring and the preservation of cultural heritage. Here, we report a chemiresistive relative humidity (RH) sensor fabricated via direct laser writing on biodegradable and rene
content: Sustainable sensing platforms are essential for environmental monitoring and the preservation of cultural heritage. Here, we report a chemiresistive relative humidity (RH) sensor fabricated via direct laser writing on biodegradable and renewable cork substrates. The sensor integrates laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrodes, a PEDOT:PSS stabilizing layer, and a hybrid of green- and chemically synthesized graphene oxide (GO) as the active sensing layer, optimizing performance while minimizing environmental impact. The device exhibits a sensitivity of 0.366 KΩ/%RH across 0–100% RH, with hysteresis below 0.5% RH, and demonstrates long-term stability with a drift of <1% RH over 75 days. Deployment in museum environments using a custom-built data logger confirmed reliable RH monitoring comparable to commercial sensors. Life cycle assessment shows that green electrolytic GO synthesis reduces climate change impact by up to 4.5-fold, while the cork substrate lowers the carbon footprint approximately eight-fold relative to polyimide-based sensors. This work presents a sustainable, high-performance RH sensing platform for real-world cultural heritage preservation applications.

title: Supplementation of tussah immunoreactive substances improves growth performance, innate immunity, and intestinal microbial homeostasis in the sea urchin Strongylocentrotus intermedius
summary: The immunomodulatory effect of tussah immunoreactive substance (TIS) on aquatic animals has been confirmed, but its probiotic effects on the sea urchin Strongylocentrotus intermedius remains unclear. A feeding experiment was carried out to
content: The immunomodulatory effect of tussah immunoreactive substance (TIS) on aquatic animals has been confirmed, but its probiotic effects on the sea urchin Strongylocentrotus intermedius remains unclear. A feeding experiment was carried out to investigate the impacts of TIS on the growth performance, innate immunity and gut microflora of S. intermedius. The results showed that 0.5% and 1.0% TIS slightly increased specific growth rate and test diameter growth rate, while all TIS treatments significantly improved the gonadosomatic index (P < 0.05). In the 1.0% TIS group, total flavor amino acids in gonads increased by 5.4%, and eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) contents were elevated by more than 10%. Also, the immune enzyme activities varied and increased to different degrees among each TIS-treated group. Proteomics analysis indicated that TIS activated immune-related genes and upregulated pathways related to mitochondrial function and energy metabolism. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that 1.0% TIS improved intestinal microbial diversity by enriching beneficial bacteria (Desulforhopalus and Ruegeria) and inhibiting harmful bacteria (Vibrio and Halarcobacter). In conclusion, dietary supplementation with TIS promotes growth, enhances immunity, and optimizes intestinal microbiota in S. intermedius. These results offer novel insights into the application of immunostimulants in sea urchin culture and contribute to the development of high-efficiency formulated feeds for sea urchins.

title: Outer membrane vesicles from Fusobacterium necrophorum elicit protective immunity in mice and robust immune responses in sheep
summary: Fusobacterium necrophorum is a major opportunistic pathogen of ruminants that causes foot rot and liver abscesses and contributes to substantial economic losses. Current vaccines provide limited protection. Here, we prepared and evaluated o
content: Fusobacterium necrophorum is a major opportunistic pathogen of ruminants that causes foot rot and liver abscesses and contributes to substantial economic losses. Current vaccines provide limited protection. Here, we prepared and evaluated outer membrane vesicles (OMVs)-based vaccine candidate derived from F. necrophorum. OMVs were purified by density-gradient centrifugation and were characterized for morphology, composition, and immunological activity. The purified OMVs showed intact vesicle structure and a uniform particle size distribution and contained virulence-associated antigens and pathogen-associated molecular patterns. OMVs were rapidly taken up by dendritic cells and promoted dendritic cell maturation, as indicated by activation of PI3K/AKT signaling and increased expression of MHC I, MHC II, CD80, and CD86. In vivo imaging showed persistent fluorescence at the injection site and signal accumulation in draining lymph nodes and the spleen. In mice, OMVs immunization induced high titers of antigen-specific IgG and elicited a Th1-biased cellular immune response. In a lethal challenge, OMVs immunization achieved 100% survival, significantly reduced liver bacterial loads, and alleviated inflammatory and necrotic liver lesions. In sheep, OMVs immunization also induced progressively increased antigen-specific IgG and a predominantly Th1 type cellular immune response, supporting strong immunogenicity in a natural host. Together, these results support F. necrophorum OMVs as a promising vaccine candidate containing multiple native antigens for the prevention and control of F. necrophorum - associated diseases in ruminants.

title: Entomopathogenic and beneficial roles of metarhizium: A review
source: International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
summary: Chemical pesticides are widely used for insect pest management, but their overuse has led to resistance, environmental contamination, and health hazards. This has created a need for effective biological alternatives, among which the genus M
content: Chemical pesticides are widely used for insect pest management, but their overuse has led to resistance, environmental contamination, and health hazards. This has created a need for effective biological alternatives, among which the genus Metarhizium (Ascomycota: Hypocreales) is notable. First described in 1879 as a cause of “green muscardine disease,” Metarhizium includes over 110 species that act as insect pathogens, soil saprobes, and plant endophytes. This review summarizes the taxonomy, biology, and infection process of Metarhizium, including adhesion, germination, and cuticle penetration, while examining the role of secondary metabolites like destruxins in virulence and safety. It highlights the genus’s applications beyond pest control, such as promoting plant growth and suppressing soil pathogens. The review also discusses formulation technologies, application methods, and challenges like shelf-life and production costs that hinder adoption. Finally, it outlines future research directions like genome editing and nano formulation to enhance the efficacy of Metarhizium-based biopesticides, showcasing its potential as a multifunctional organism in sustainable agriculture.

title: Advances in scientific production technology & post harvest management of Tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.)
source: International Journal of Research in Agronomy
summary: Tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.), an extremely versatile tropical fruit tree belonging to the family Fabaceae (Subfamily: Caesalpinioideae), is indigenous to tropical Africa but is grown in India since ages. Being adaptable, long-lived, nutr
content: Tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.), an extremely versatile tropical fruit tree belonging to the family Fabaceae (Subfamily: Caesalpinioideae), is indigenous to tropical Africa but is grown in India since ages. Being adaptable, long-lived, nutritious, medicinal and industrial, it has become one of the important fruit crops in the world. India is the largest producer as well as consumer of tamarind.
