A systematic literature review identified 233 practices, which were consolidated into a taxonomy of 33 CE practices organized into five hierarchical categories based on value preservation: food surplus prevention, avoidable waste prevention, reuse, recycling, and recovery. An Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA) assessed specialists' perceptions of the strategic importance and implementation of each practice. The findings indicate that, although CE practices were consistently perceived as highly important in both countries, their implementation differed substantially. Higher implementation levels in Spain were associated with a more consolidated regulatory environment, technological infrastructure, and coordinated governance, whereas wider implementation gaps in Brazil were linked to technological limitations and institutional fragmentation. This study contributes by systematizing retail-oriented CE practices into an integrated taxonomy, operationalizing the distinction between food surplus prevention and avoidable waste prevention, and showing how institutional conditions shape the adoption of CE practices. The findings provide practical guidance for retailers in prioritizing circular interventions and inform policymakers on institutional actions needed to accelerate food waste prevention and support progress toward Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12.3.

title: CFD Simulation of Cryogenic LH₂ Refuelling with Boil-Off Management
summary: ABSTRACT Cryogenic liquid hydrogen (LH₂) is emerging as a key enabler for zero-emission transport in aerospace and heavy-duty mobility. Simulating LH₂ refuelling is essential for system design and safety, yet remains challenging due to tigh
content: ABSTRACT Cryogenic liquid hydrogen (LH₂) is emerging as a key enabler for zero-emission transport in aerospace and heavy-duty mobility. Simulating LH₂ refuelling is essential for system design and safety, yet remains challenging due to tightly coupled multiphase phenomena, rapid thermodynamic transients, and limited experimental data. This study presents a high-fidelity 3D CFD methodology for transient LH₂ refuelling under realistic operating conditions. The model combines the Volume of Fluid (VOF) approach with the Lee phase-change formulation and finely resolved real-gas property (RGP) tables derived from NIST data to ensure thermodynamic accuracy near the saturation line. A staged initialization, automatic mesh adaption, adaptive time stepping, and automated boil-off control enable stable and computationally efficient resolution of thermal, flow, and interface dynamics. Inlet boundary conditions are based on measured mass flow rates from an actual LH₂ refuelling campaign, thereby ensuring realistic model input. A dedicated sensitivity study demonstrates that the predicted pressure evolution is strongly affected by the Lee phase-change coefficients, particularly the condensation coefficient, highlighting the need for application-specific calibration. The physical plausibility of the model is supported by comparison with a lumped phase-equilibrium approach, while validation against NASA LH₂ refuelling experiments shows good agreement in the characteristic pressure evolution and liquid fill level. Overall, the developed workflow provides a robust, transferable, and extensible framework for modelling cryogenic LH₂ refuelling and supports future model refinement, parameter calibration, and the optimization and safety assessment of hydrogen storage and refuelling systems in both research and industrial applications.

title: Rethinking chemical clusters: Greenfield and brownfield transition to net-zero by 2050
summary: We develop a cluster-level optimization framework to design brownfield transition pathways toward net-zero chemical clusters by 2050, applied to existing ammonia-olefin clusters in the Netherlands. The model represents sequential investment
content: We develop a cluster-level optimization framework to design brownfield transition pathways toward net-zero chemical clusters by 2050, applied to existing ammonia-olefin clusters in the Netherlands. The model represents sequential investment decisions for 2030, 2040, and 2050, includes scope 1–3 emissions, and enables a systematic comparison of greenfield and brownfield configurations. Thirteen olefin and eight ammonia production routes are considered. The results show that, despite reduced flexibility due to legacy assets, net-zero brownfield configurations remain feasible. Plastic gasification combined with methanol-to-olefins emerges as a low-regret option for olefins, while electric steam methane reforming and electrolyzers are robust choices for ammonia. The results support early investment rather than strategic delay. Excluding scope 3 emissions leads to lock-in of fossil-based options that appear cost-effective short-term but raise long-term system costs. Sensitivity analyses highlight uncertainties related to infrastructure and technology availability, bio-feedstock prices, and plastic waste emission accounting.

title: Predictive and Explainable Modeling of Dialysis Membranes: Linking Structure–Surface Modifiers to Transport Mechanisms, Fouling Behavior, and Mass Transfer Resistances
summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) highlights the ongoing need to improve dialyzer performance by enhancing clearance, biocompatibility, and reducing fouling. In this study, four types of membrane modifiers (pore forming (PF), antioxidant (AO), a
content: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) highlights the ongoing need to improve dialyzer performance by enhancing clearance, biocompatibility, and reducing fouling. In this study, four types of membrane modifiers (pore forming (PF), antioxidant (AO), antifouling (AF), and anticoagulant (AC)) were evaluated for their effects on structural and functional properties. Incorporation of PF increased porosity by 9% and promoted uniform pore distribution, reducing flux decline by 11% and improving long-term stability. AO, by enlarging pore size and enhancing antioxidant properties, achieved the greatest performance improvement, increasing urea clearance by 16%, water flux by 19%, convective contribution by 28%, and lowering membrane mass-transfer resistance by 27%. AF reduced surface roughness, decreased protein adsorption by 50%, stabilized flux, and lowered total resistance by 18%. Similarly, AC enhanced flow uniformity and biocompatibility by decreasing contact resistance with blood and dialysate by 6.7% and 4.2%, respectively. Despite these improvements, the influence of these modifiers on fouling mechanisms, water and urea flux, clearance, and mass transfer resistances had not been comprehensively examined. To address this, modeling and sensitivity analyses were performed. Comparison with classical mass transfer models indicated that PF and AC created more uniform structures, enhancing diffusion stability and reducing deviation, while AO and AF increased porosity and widened transport pathways, promoting convective and diffusive transfer. Pareto and SHAP analyses highlighted the dominant role of AO in urea clearance and water flux. Overall, concurrent modification of membrane surface and structure improved filtration outcomes and provided deeper mechanistic insight, while modeling yielded higher predictive accuracy than previous studies.

title: Review of Technical Developments in Direct Injection of Ammonia for Engines With Assessment of Spray, Combustion, and Emission Characteristics
summary: The global transition from fossil fuels to carbon‐free energy has accelerated interest in renewable fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia (NH 3 ). Ammonia has emerged as a promising carbon‐free energy carrier because it can be liquefied at app
content: The global transition from fossil fuels to carbon‐free energy has accelerated interest in renewable fuels such as hydrogen and ammonia (NH 3 ). Ammonia has emerged as a promising carbon‐free energy carrier because it can be liquefied at approximately 1 MPa under ambient conditions, has a high‐octane number of about 110, and contains 17.6 wt% hydrogen, making it attractive for large‐scale energy storage and transportation. This article focuses on earlier research and recent studies on technical developments in direct injection (DI) of NH 3 ‐assisted combustion. Focus on the combustion characteristics of NH 3 DI in ICEs, as well as the spray characteristics, safety, and handling of NH 3 . This review paper develops the fundamentals of the mechanism of NH 3 combustion technology, providing new insights into the application of NH 3 in ICEs. Although NH 3 possesses favorable storage characteristics, its application in ICEs is challenged by a high autoignition temperature ( ∼ 650 °C), low laminar flame speed ( ∼ 7 cm/s), and lower heating value (18.8 MJ/kg), which contribute to combustion instability, NO x formation, and NH 3 slip. The review also explains the fundamental combustion mechanisms of ammonia and identifies key research gaps and future directions for developing efficient, low‐emission ammonia‐fueled internal combustion engines, supporting the transition towards sustainable and carbon‐free transportation.

title: Life-cycle management of nitrogen fertilizer systems in China reduces greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen pollution while improving air quality
summary: Nitrogen fertilizers sustain food security but complicate climate and air-pollution mitigation. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions arise mainly from energy-intensive production, whereas reactive nitrogen (Nr) losses occur largely during applica
content: Nitrogen fertilizers sustain food security but complicate climate and air-pollution mitigation. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions arise mainly from energy-intensive production, whereas reactive nitrogen (Nr) losses occur largely during application. Here, we develop an integrated life-cycle framework that links fertilizer production and cropland nitrogen budgets and apply it to China for 1990–2020. Expanding fertilizer exports widens the disconnect between production and application. In 2020, the system emitted 432 Tg CO 2 eq and 3.3 Tg Nr, increasing PM 2.5 concentrations by up to 5.2 μg m −3 across central and eastern China. Production accounted for 77% of GHG emissions, while application caused 92% of Nr losses. Coordinated management could reduce GHG emissions by 65% and Nr losses by 52% by 2050, lower PM 2.5 concentrations by 1.5 μg m −3 , and avoid approximately 195,000 premature deaths. These results show that life-cycle coordination is essential for unlocking mitigation synergies in fertilizer systems.

title: Evaluating the Environmental Benefits of 3D Printing Based Part Production for Low-volume Automotive Applications
source: Journal of the Korean Society for Precision Engineering
summary: 3D printing is emerging as a promising solution for the automotive industry, as it offers economic advantages in smallbatch, high-variety production and mitigates climate impact by eliminating mold fabrication. This study compares the carbo
content: 3D printing is emerging as a promising solution for the automotive industry, as it offers economic advantages in smallbatch, high-variety production and mitigates climate impact by eliminating mold fabrication. This study compares the carbonemission reduction potential and economic feasibility of fused deposition modeling (FDM)—the most widely used polymer 3D printing process—with those of conventional injection molding at the actual component level. The analysis shows that the environmental burden of mold manufacturing in injection molding is substantial, confirming the advantage of FDM in low-volume production. Specifically, for production volumes below 645 units, FDM performs better in reducing carbon emissions. These findings indicate that FDM can serve as a sustainable alternative for low-volume manufacturing in automotive applications.

title: CT imaging-based analysis of nonlinear flow in fragmented rock accumulations for smart CO₂ sequestration in mining goafs
summary: ABSTRACT In response to the global push for carbon neutrality, green mining technologies such as CO 2 sequestration in abandoned goaf areas have emerged as promising Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) pathways. However, fragmen
content: ABSTRACT In response to the global push for carbon neutrality, green mining technologies such as CO 2 sequestration in abandoned goaf areas have emerged as promising Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) pathways. However, fragmented rock accumulations in goafs exhibit complex nonlinear flow characteristics owing to their heterogeneous void structures, thereby challenging traditional seepage models. This study leverages advanced Computed Tomography (CT) imaging technology to reconstruct realistic three-dimensional rock models and employs a progressive laminar-turbulent coupling Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) approach to investigate the seepage behavior across varying flow velocities. A modified nonlinear seepage equation was proposed that incorporates dimensionless parameters to enhance the accuracy of the Ergun equation. The results demonstrate that compaction intensifies flow irregularities, triggering nonlinear effects at low critical Reynolds numbers (1–5), which decrease correspondingly with decreasing porosity and exhibit a strong negative correlation. These findings underscore the limitations of Darcy’s Law. Vortex formation at low velocities in highly compact assemblies results in significant energy dissipation. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for smart CO 2 storage strategies for goafs to promote efficient and safe green mining practices.

title: Integrated framework for holistic student development: physical literacy, nutrition, and playground design in ASEAN
source: Sportis Scientific Journal of School Sport Physical Education and Psychomotricity
summary: Holistic student development in ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) educational contexts demands integrated approaches that simultaneously address physical literacy, nutrition literacy, and supportive play environments. This stud
content: Holistic student development in ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) educational contexts demands integrated approaches that simultaneously address physical literacy, nutrition literacy, and supportive play environments. This study aimed to develop and empirically validate an integrated physical literacy, nutrition literacy, and playground-based framework. A four-phase sequential mixed-methods design was applied, including expert consultation, document analysis, prototype development, and quantitative validation. Construct validation involved 1415 elementary students and was analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and structural equation modeling. Students demonstrated high levels of holistic development (M = 78.2), physical literacy (M = 76.4), creativity in play (M = 74.3), and nutrition literacy (M = 72.1), with daily physical activity showing moderate levels (M = 68.9). All predictor variables were significantly associated with holistic student development (r = 0.69–0.77, p < 0.01), with creativity in play emerging as the strongest correlate. The findings provide robust empirical support for the integrated multidimensional framework as an integrated, culturally responsive model for enhancing children’s physical, cognitive, and socio-emotional development.

title: Mapping carbon intensities of circular battery and hydrogen technologies as key players in carbon-neutral transitions
summary: Global transitions toward battery and hydrogen circular economies are key pieces of sustainable development goals (SDGs). As driving forces for SDGs, battery and hydrogen technologies have been globally studied and applied, but basic indica
content: Global transitions toward battery and hydrogen circular economies are key pieces of sustainable development goals (SDGs). As driving forces for SDGs, battery and hydrogen technologies have been globally studied and applied, but basic indicators on life-cycle carbon intensity and operating carbon emissions have not been consistently provided. This leads to (1) unclear carbon emission and decarbonization quantifications, (2) unknown differences in technology development maturity and technical readiness levels across regions, and (3) disparities in carbon intensity mapping for battery and hydrogen circular economies. To this end, this paper systematically summarizes and analyzes battery and hydrogen circular economies, emphasizing (1) life-cycle carbon intensity models, (2) the impact of advanced battery and hydrogen technology innovations on multicountry decarbonization estimates, and (3) the application prospects indicated by carbon intensity. This perspective provides researchers with a route toward a carbon intensity database and dynamic carbon intensity accounting, with the aim to provide a quantifiable core method to guide the verifiable carbon neutrality transition of batteries and hydrogen circular economies.

title: Optimizing CO2 capture: Integrating membrane-based separation with conventional methods for enhanced performance
source: Chemical Engineering Journal Green and Sustainable
summary: The global increase in CO 2 emissions necessitates the development of efficient and sustainable carbon capture technologies. This review explores the integration of membrane-based separation with conventional CO 2 capture methods, such as a
content: The global increase in CO 2 emissions necessitates the development of efficient and sustainable carbon capture technologies. This review explores the integration of membrane-based separation with conventional CO 2 capture methods, such as absorption, adsorption, and cryogenic, forming hybrid processes. These hybrid approaches aim to optimize CO 2 capture performance by leveraging the strengths of each method, while addressing their inherent limitations. Membrane technology, known for its high selectivity and energy efficiency, when combined with other capture processes, enhances the CO 2 recovery rates, reduces energy consumption, and improves process stability. This work discusses the synthesis of membrane-based porous supports and the solvents used in hybrid CO 2 capture processes, their CO 2 capture performance, integration benefits, and capture mechanisms. Furthermore, the review identifies key research gaps and provides insights into future directions for achieving scalable and practical applications of hybrid membrane-based CO 2 capture systems.

title: Adaptation practices to climate change through crisis management: Evidence from farmers in Japan
summary: Natural disasters driven by climate change are increasingly frequent, directly affecting the agricultural sector. Developing farm management strategies to adapt to climate change is critical for maintaining stable agricultural production. T
content: Natural disasters driven by climate change are increasingly frequent, directly affecting the agricultural sector. Developing farm management strategies to adapt to climate change is critical for maintaining stable agricultural production. This study aims to explore how Japanese farmers adapt to climate change-related crises through crisis management. Data were collected from 232 Japanese farmers and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The Farmers' Adaptation to Climate Change model was developed based on Mitroff's crisis management theory. The findings indicate that Japanese farmers have a relatively moderate perception of climate change (70% of respondents). Regarding the relationship between cultivation adaptation and managerial options, the results indicate that farmers tend to implement individual adaptation measures rather than integrate them into a comprehensive managerial-level strategy in response to climate change-related damage. Adaptation practice is often undertaken in a haphazard and there are insufficient managerial options in place to ensure sustainable implementation. Enhancing the effectiveness and sustainability of adaptation practices requires accumulating experience related to climate change-induced damage and institutionalizing it as systematic knowledge within the farm management system. To facilitate the adoption of climate-conscious practices, it is necessary to provide farmers with incentives that offset the lack of direct profitability inherent in mitigation activities.

title: Deflagration-to-detonation transition control in coal-based gas–solid mixtures: effects of tube diameter and PTFE film thickness
summary: ABSTRACT This work investigates deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT) control and pulse-detonation performance of coal-based gas–solid mixtures in a modular coaxial annular pulse detonation combustor (PDC). The primary effects of comb
content: ABSTRACT This work investigates deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT) control and pulse-detonation performance of coal-based gas–solid mixtures in a modular coaxial annular pulse detonation combustor (PDC). The primary effects of combustion chamber inner diameter and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) film thickness on detonation initiation, peak pressure, and heat release rate (HRR) were quantified through two-phase numerical simulations and high-speed pressure array experiments. Results show that larger inner diameters promote flame-surface growth and transverse-wave formation, enabling earlier shock–flame coupling and self-sustained detonation. The effect of PTFE thickness is non-monotonic: excessive thickness suppresses propagation, while moderate thickness (3 mm) offers the best trade-off between detonation triggering and stability. A regression analysis linking equivalence ratio, coal heating value, and particle size to combustion efficiency achieves high predictive accuracy ( R ²≈0.997), indicating benefits of moderately fuel-rich operation and finer particles. Among coal ranks, bituminous coal demonstrates superior performance. Two-phase simulations with calibrated kinetic models accurately reproduce Chapman-Jouguet states and agree well with measured wave speeds and pressures. The findings provide quantitative guidance for co-optimizing combustor geometry, PTFE film thickness, and fuel preparation to enhance DDT performance, supporting coal-participating detonation propulsion and mining applications.

title: Air-Breathing Polymer Electrolyte Fuel Cells: A Critical Review of Recent Progress and Future Research Needs
summary: Air-breathing polymer electrolyte fuel cells (PEFCs) are a simplified alternative to conventional forced-convection PEFC systems, eliminating external air-supply devices to reduce system complexity, weight, and cost, and to minimise parasit
content: Air-breathing polymer electrolyte fuel cells (PEFCs) are a simplified alternative to conventional forced-convection PEFC systems, eliminating external air-supply devices to reduce system complexity, weight, and cost, and to minimise parasitic losses. Despite these advantages, their passive configuration poses critical challenges in oxygen mass transport, water management, thermal regulation, and environmental sensitivity. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric and systematic review of air-breathing PEFC research published between 2000 and 2025. Using the Scopus database and a PRISMA-guided screening framework, 224 relevant documents were analysed through the Bibliometrix package in RStudio and VOSviewer to map publication trends, international collaborations, keyword evolution, and thematic research clusters. The results indicate irregular but sustained growth in research output, with an annual growth rate of 8.67%. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified major research themes centred on water management, gas diffusion layer optimisation, flow-field design, numerical modelling, thermal diagnostics, and durability enhancement. Emerging niches include piezoelectric-assisted mass transport and advanced membrane materials for high-temperature and miniature systems. The findings highlight that future technological progress depends on improved mass-transport engineering, enhanced membrane stability, optimised passive flow architectures, and integrated stack-level thermal management. For researchers, the study clarifies the field's conceptual evolution and highlights the most critical research gaps. For industry stakeholders, it provides strategic insights into design priorities for compact, reliable hydrogen-powered systems suitable for portable, off-grid, and unmanned aerial vehicle applications.

title: Breakthrough in Microwave Absorption for Long‐Term Thermal Cycling (HfZrTiCe‐Ln)C/SiC With Dual‐Heterogeneous Interfaces
source: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
summary: ABSTRACT The dielectric loss mechanism for the broadband absorption performance of carbide ceramics has not yet been elucidated, due to the long‐standing difficulty in obtaining zero‐amorphous carbon interfaces. Here, we applied a machine l
content: ABSTRACT The dielectric loss mechanism for the broadband absorption performance of carbide ceramics has not yet been elucidated, due to the long‐standing difficulty in obtaining zero‐amorphous carbon interfaces. Here, we applied a machine learning compositional design system to accelerate the discovery of high‐performance materials. An interface engineering strategy was then proposed to understand high‐performance microwave absorbers based on (HfZrTiCe‐La/Nd/Gd)C‐ceramic composites, which was assisted by using lattice matching effect of SiC and variable valence rare earth elements. The mono‐heterogeneous interface of SiC/HEC composite without carbon phases, formed via diffusion‐driven solid‐phase reactions, were first observed. HRTEM observations and MD simulations confirmed that SiC/C/HEC formed dual‐heterogeneous carbon interfaces (SiC‐graphite and HEC‐amorphous carbon). The latter composites showed superior effective absorption bandwidth and reflection loss in the frequency range of 2–18 GHz compared to the former composites. Specifically, effective absorption bandwidth of the SiC/C/HEC‐La was 7.5 GHz at 2.2 mm, which is 15 times that of SiC/HEC‐La. This was owing to the former with 73.14% proportion of sp3/sp2 carbon bonds and a higher interfacial carbon content, which improved dielectric loss and impedance matching. The dual‐heterogeneous carbon interface, having over half of the disordered carbon phase ( I D / I G = 1.14) is the key factor.

title: Enabling high-performance transparent photovoltaics through atomic layer deposition techniques
summary: Transparent photovoltaics (TPVs) offer a promising pathway for integrating solar energy harvesting into windows, façades, greenhouses, and wearable electronics while preserving visible-light transmission. However, achieving a balance betwee
content: Transparent photovoltaics (TPVs) offer a promising pathway for integrating solar energy harvesting into windows, façades, greenhouses, and wearable electronics while preserving visible-light transmission. However, achieving a balance between power-conversion efficiency, transparency, color neutrality, and long-term stability remains a major challenge. This article critically examines the role of atomic layer deposition (ALD) as an enabling technology for addressing these limitations in organic, perovskite, dye-sensitized, silicon-based, and tandem transparent photovoltaic systems. Particular emphasis is placed on ALD-enabled transport layers, interface engineering, defect passivation, carrier-selective contacts, and encapsulation strategies. The mechanisms by which ALD suppresses interfacial recombination, improves band alignment, mitigates ion migration, and enhances environmental stability are critically discussed. The advantages and limitations of ALD are evaluated through comparative analysis with other thin-film deposition techniques, highlighting its suitability for ultrathin functional layers and interface engineering. Finally, remaining challenges related to cost, throughput, precursor development, and scalability are evaluated, together with emerging opportunities offered by plasma-enhanced, spatial, atmospheric-pressure, and roll-to-roll ALD for large-area TPVs commercialization.

title: Effect of Transition Metal Ions on the Reactive Crystallization and Morphology of Lithium Carbonate
summary: ABSTRACT The increasing demand for lithium‐ion batteries has intensified the importance of lithium carbonate, whose crystallization behavior, morphology, and filtration characteristics are influenced by crystallization conditions and transi
content: ABSTRACT The increasing demand for lithium‐ion batteries has intensified the importance of lithium carbonate, whose crystallization behavior, morphology, and filtration characteristics are influenced by crystallization conditions and transition‐metal impurities, particularly Ni 2+ , Co 2+ , and Mn 2+ . In this study, the effects of these ions on the reactive crystallization of lithium carbonate were systematically investigated. Crystal morphology and phase composition were characterized using SEM, FESEM‐EDS, XRD, and FTIR, while zeta potential measurements were performed to evaluate surface charge, and TGA was used to assess thermal decomposition behavior. The results showed that the presence of Co 2+ promoted more compact, rounded crystals with smoother surfaces, whereas Ni 2+ induced elongated, thin, plate‐like structures with increased surface irregularity. Mn 2+ resulted in intermediate shapes. Zeta potential measurements revealed a significant increase in surface charge in the presence of metal ions, enhancing electrostatic repulsion and reducing particle aggregation. Filtration behavior was also significantly influenced by crystal morphology: crystals formed in pure media exhibited the highest specific cake resistance, whereas Co 2+ and Mn 2+ substantially improved filterability by producing more permeable filter cakes, while Ni 2+ showed a moderate effect. These findings highlight the critical role of transition‐metal impurities in regulating lithium carbonate crystallization, crystal properties, and filtration performance.

title: Do green innovation and resilience mediate the relationship between AI-enabled dynamic capabilities and sustainable supply chain performance?
summary: Despite recent advances in the deployment of artificial intelligence technologies for building resilient industries and sustainable development, existing literature largely overlooks the dual mediation role of green innovation and supply ch
content: Despite recent advances in the deployment of artificial intelligence technologies for building resilient industries and sustainable development, existing literature largely overlooks the dual mediation role of green innovation and supply chain resilience in how AI-enabled dynamic capabilities relate to the sustainable performance of supply chains. In this study, we extend the dynamic capabilities framework by integrating AI-enabled dynamic capabilities and these two mediator variables in influencing sustainable supply chain performance. Drawing on survey data collected from 634 managers in 423 Chinese construction firms, our empirical validation demonstrates that AI-enabled dynamic capabilities amplify businesses' capacity to sense, seize, and reconfigure resources more rapidly in complex environments. Both green innovation and supply chain resilience exert significant mediation effects. Our theoretical contribution lies in showing that green innovation proactively enhances environmental performance through sustainable practices while supply chain resilience ensures reactive adaptability amid disruptions. These findings offer important implications for how construction industry firms should strategically invest in AI-enabled dynamic capabilities to meet new regulatory requirements, foster sustainable competitive advantages and build resilient supply chains.

title: Ion‐Ligand Synergistic Strategy Enhancing Optical Performance of Perovskite Nanocrystals for Wide Color Gamut Display
summary: ABSTRACT Halide perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) are promising emitters for wide‐color‐gamut displays owing to their high color purity, yet their practical application is limited by ligand desorption‐induced instability. Here, we develop a seq
content: ABSTRACT Halide perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) are promising emitters for wide‐color‐gamut displays owing to their high color purity, yet their practical application is limited by ligand desorption‐induced instability. Here, we develop a sequential ion‐ligand synergistic passivation strategy to stabilize CsPbBr 3 NCs. Zn 2+ ions are introduced to compensate surface Pb vacancies, while thiol ligands further passivate undercoordinated Pb/Zn sites, thereby reducing surface defects and enhancing lattice stability. The resulting NCs exhibit a narrower emission spectra and high photoluminescence quantum yield of ∼95% together with significantly improved optical stability, demonstrating the advantages of sequential ion‐ligand synergistic strategy. Further encapsulation into PMMA microspheres efficiently enhances environmental robustness of NCs, enabling a T 85 lifetime approximately sevenfold longer than that of pristine NCs under 85°C/85% RH conditions. The resultant white light‐emitting diodes based on NCs microspheres achieve ∼121% of NTSC color gamut with a superior display performance and excellent long‐term operation stability. Therefore, this work establishes a synergistic ion‐ligand passivation strategy for stabilizing perovskite NCs and offers a design strategy for high‐performance display applications.

title: Oncologic Safety and Viability of Stem Cell-Enriched Autologous Fat Grafting: A Narrative Review of the Preclinical and Clinical Evidence
source: International Journal of Medical Science and Clinical Research Studies
summary: Autologous fat grafting has become a cornerstone of both reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgery, yet unpredictable resorption of the transplanted tissue remains its principal technical limitation. This has driven the development of en
content: Autologous fat grafting has become a cornerstone of both reconstructive and aesthetic plastic surgery, yet unpredictable resorption of the transplanted tissue remains its principal technical limitation. This has driven the development of enrichment strategies in which the lipoaspirate is supplemented with the stromal vascular fraction or with culture-expanded adipose-derived stem/stromal cells (ADSCs). Enrichment consistently improves graft retention in most clinical series, but ADSCs are also potent secretors of angiogenic, mitogenic and immunomodulatory mediators, which raises a legitimate concern: could the same biology that keeps a graft alive also awaken or accelerate residual tumor cells in the recipient bed? This narrative review synthesizes the current in vitro, animal and clinical evidence on the oncologic safety and technical viability of stem cell-enriched fat transfer, with emphasis on breast reconstruction after oncologic surgery. Laboratory studies remain frankly contradictory, describing both tumor-promoting and tumor-suppressive effects that appear to depend on the donor, the cell subpopulation, the tumor molecular subtype and the experimental model. In vivo animal work is similarly divided, although several models suggest that whole fat graft is a less permissive environment for tumor engraftment than the isolated cell fraction. In contrast, clinical series, matched cohorts and multicenter studies including several thousand patients have not demonstrated an increase in locoregional recurrence, systemic recurrence or second primary tumors attributable to either conventional or enriched fat grafting. The available evidence supports the continued use of enriched lipotransfer in patients who have completed oncologic treatment and show no evidence of active disease, provided that informed consent, structured imaging follow-up and prospective data collection are incorporated into routine practice.

title: Catalytic Cracking of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons with Hydrogen Transfer Reaction in the RFCC Process
source: Journal of the Japan Petroleum Institute
summary: Residue fluid catalytic cracking (RFCC) is a crucial technology for converting heavy oils into valuable light fractions. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in heavy oils have conventionally been regarded as stable and difficult to crac
content: Residue fluid catalytic cracking (RFCC) is a crucial technology for converting heavy oils into valuable light fractions. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in heavy oils have conventionally been regarded as stable and difficult to crack, but we found that decomposition can proceed through hydrogen transfer reactions with coexisting substances, such as naphthenes, paraffins, and aromatic ring side chains. This article introduces our research findings on the catalytic cracking of PAHs in the RFCC process specifically the effects of the number of aromatic rings, types of coexisting substances, and composition and degradation states of the catalyst on PAH conversion. Based on detailed product analyses, the reaction pathways and rate-determining steps were also determined. Furthermore, we discuss the development of an interpretable machine learning model to predict product compositions and extract key reaction factors for catalytic cracking with complex feedstocks. This model provides data-driven evidence that the interaction between hydrogen donors and PAHs contributes to both suppression of coke formation and promotion of decomposition. These findings are expected to enhance heavy oil upgrading efficiencies in petroleum refining.

title: Drastic Biodiversity Transition as a Function of Rainfall Patterns: From Coastal Drylands to Amazonian Rainforests
summary: ABSTRACT Aim By moving beyond traditional biome‐centric approaches to sample continuously across a massive ecotone, we investigate how species richness, community composition, and dominance of woody plants change across a strong longitudina
content: ABSTRACT Aim By moving beyond traditional biome‐centric approaches to sample continuously across a massive ecotone, we investigate how species richness, community composition, and dominance of woody plants change across a strong longitudinal precipitation gradient and identify thresholds in water availability that drive shifts in community assembly between tropical dry forests and rainforests. Location A longitudinal precipitation gradient within and beyond the Marañon Valley, a biogeographic corridor linking Pacific dryland forests, Andean highland forests, and Amazon rainforests in northern Peru. Time Period Contemporary forests sampled between 2016 and 2020. Major Taxa Studied Woody tree species (angiosperms). Methods We modelled species richness, community composition, and species dominance in response to climatic and edaphic factors using floristic data from the first National Forest Inventory in Peru. Results Alpha diversity increased from the coastal drylands to the Andes, peaking at a 1299 mm annual precipitation threshold. Beyond this threshold in the Amazon, climatic factors no longer explain diversity patterns. Species composition shifted gradually, exhibiting sharp regional differences at 1265 mm. Species dominance patterns changed markedly along the longitudinal axis, from locally dominant, stress‐adapted species in drylands to regionally widespread low‐dominant species in the Amazon Forest. Main Conclusions Our findings indicate that major transitions in woody plant biodiversity are tightly linked to rainfall patterns up to a critical threshold, beyond which other factors likely govern community structure, highlighting the vulnerability and potential reorganization of these ecosystems under ongoing climatic change. Ultimately, this demonstrates that assessing the landscape as a continuum, rather than exploring isolated biomes, is crucial for capturing the non‐linear environmental thresholds that redefine community assembly rules on a global scale.

title: Promoting synergistic development of wind power hydrogen production system and fuel cell vehicle in China: A subjective game perspective
source: Energy Sources Part B Economics Planning and Policy
summary: Driven by the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, the synergistic development of a wind power hydrogen production system (WPHPS) and fuel cell vehicle (FCV) constitutes a pathway to lower wind curtailment and reduce carbon emissions
content: Driven by the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, the synergistic development of a wind power hydrogen production system (WPHPS) and fuel cell vehicle (FCV) constitutes a pathway to lower wind curtailment and reduce carbon emissions in the transportation sector. This study investigates the evolutionary process of strategic behaviors between WPHPS and FCV based on a subjective game model, conducts empirical analysis in China, analyzes four regions’ heterogeneity, and conducts sensitivity analysis of core factors, including subsidy policies, hydrogen prices, and hydrogen demand. The results indicate that: (1) the evolutionary process of strategic behaviors presents dynamic characteristics of “cognitive accumulation – strategy sets expansion – equilibrium reconstruction.” When the game reaches a long-term stable equilibrium, the probabilities of “both parties cooperate” and “both parties do not cooperate” stabilize at 0.3729 and 0.1998, respectively; (2) regional heterogeneity influences the strategic behaviors and game equilibrium. Supported by high hydrogen prices and comprehensive subsidies, Southern China achieves the highest cooperation probability of 0.7102, ranking first, followed by North and Central China, East China, and Northwest China, with cooperation probabilities of 0.3923, 0.3362, and 0.3298, respectively; and (3) The sensitivity order of the core factors affecting the cooperation probability is hydrogen price, demand, and subsidy policy. This study expands the application boundary of subjective game theory in the field of WPHPS and FCV, and provides practical implications for market mechanism optimization and policy formulation.

title: Integrated glycerol biorefinery: volatile fatty acid platform for polyhydroxyalkanoates production under feast/famine operation
summary: This study evaluated aerobic (Stage 1) and anaerobic (Stage 2) feeding strategies in a sequencing batch reactor (SBR) for polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) accumulation, using fermented effluent from a glycerol-fed acidogenic reactor operated at h
content: This study evaluated aerobic (Stage 1) and anaerobic (Stage 2) feeding strategies in a sequencing batch reactor (SBR) for polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) accumulation, using fermented effluent from a glycerol-fed acidogenic reactor operated at hydraulic retention times (HRT) of 4 and 8 days. Coordinating upstream acidogenic fermentation with downstream reactor feeding strategies is necessary to enhance carbon conversion within biorefinery concepts. Extending the acidogenic HRT from 4 to 8 days increased volatile fatty acid (VFA) production to 3167 mg COD/L (a 21% increase), reduced residual glycerol, and shifted the metabolic profile from a predominance of acetic and butyric acids to butyric and caproic acids. In feast/famine SBR operations, representative cycles showed that PHA accumulated faster under anaerobic feeding (Stage 2), reaching 10.0 mg PHA/L after 2 h compared to 7.5 mg PHA/L under aerobic feeding (Stage 1). Stage 2 also achieved a volumetric productivity of 59.77 mg PHA/L/h and specific yields of 0.37 g PHA/g VFA and 0.64 g PHA/g glycerol, outperforming Stage 1 yields of 0.28 and 0.20 g/g, respectively. Although the higher concentration of medium-chain carboxylic acids did not result in a corresponding increase in downstream polymer accumulation, the operational feeding strategy was the primary determinant of performance. These experimental findings provide robustness to the concept of coupling upstream acidogenesis with downstream PHA production, demonstrating how integrating anaerobic feeding with a prolonged HRT improves carbon conversion yields from a glycerol substrate.

title: Clean H2 production at room temperature using CuPd/TiO2 catalytic hypophosphite hydrolysis
summary: A safe, clean, and cost-effective H2 production system is critically important for developing hydrogen energy. Sodium hypophosphite (NHP) represents a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high stability, low cost, and abundance. NHP can hy
content: A safe, clean, and cost-effective H2 production system is critically important for developing hydrogen energy. Sodium hypophosphite (NHP) represents a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high stability, low cost, and abundance. NHP can hydrolyse under mild conditions to yield H2 without any gaseous by-products. In this work, we report clean and efficient H2 production at room temperature using CuPd/TiO2 catalytic NHP hydrolysis with the rate of 13.53 mL·min−1 (135.3 mL·min−1·g−1) and 100% NHP conversion within 30 min. The catalyst also exhibits excellent recyclability toward H2 production. The two metals in CuPd/TiO2 exhibit a synergistic effect, Cu can facilitate the activation and dissociation of water, whereas Pd sites accelerate the activation and dehydrogenation of H2PO2−. This work develops a new cost-economic and highly efficient catalytic H2 production system, which is expected to contribute to development of hydrogen economy. Sodium hypophosphite (NHP) represents a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high stability, low cost and abundance, however, its potential as a source for hydrogen production remains underexplored. Here, the authors report a room-temperature, additive-free, hydrogen production system based on NHP and water as carriers and CuPd/TiO2 as a catalyst, with NHP reaching 100% conversion within 30 min and a hydrogen production rate of 135.3 mL·min−1·g−1.

title: Selective ethanol detection using SmFe1−xCoxO3 p-type perovskite oxide semiconductors
source: Journal of the Ceramic Society of Japan
summary: This study investigates the effects of cobalt (Co) substitution in SmFe1−xCoxO3 perovskite oxides on the sensing property of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). The introduction of Co induces a hole-doping effect, increasing electrical condu
content: This study investigates the effects of cobalt (Co) substitution in SmFe1−xCoxO3 perovskite oxides on the sensing property of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). The introduction of Co induces a hole-doping effect, increasing electrical conductivity and enabling lower operating temperatures, thereby improving VOC selectivity. SmFe1−xCoxO3 powders were synthesized via the glycothermal method and characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area measurements. Gas sensing properties were evaluated for ethanol and toluene at varying temperatures and concentrations. The results indicate that Co substitution significantly influences oxidation activity and electrical resistance, thereby modifying gas sensing behavior. The SmFe1−xCoxO3 sensor with x = 0.1 exhibited the highest selectivity of Sethanol/Stoluene = 5.89 at 250 °C toward ethanol over toluene, attributed to an optimal balance between electrical conductivity and oxidation activity. Co substitution enhanced the oxidation activities for ethanol and toluene, and the difference in the 50 % conversion temperatures (T50) between ethanol and toluene increased with increasing Co content (x). Additionally, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to gain further insight into the gas sensing mechanism. Surface adsorption energies and electronic interactions of ethanol and toluene on SmFe1−xCoxO3 were analyzed, revealing that the formation of oxygen vacancy due to the Co substitution selectively increases the adsorption strength of ethanol. This study highlights the potential of Co-substituted SmFeO3 as a selective ethanol sensor with lower operating temperatures and enhanced detection capabilities. The findings contribute to the development of advanced perovskite-based gas sensors with improved efficiency and selectivity for real-world applications.

title: The PESTEL framework and its variants for analysing the strategic environment: Evolution, limitations and adoption in energy policy research
summary: This paper examines the evolution and critique of the PESTEL framework (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Ecological, Legal) and its variants for macro-environment analyses. Variants include DESTEP, ETPS, LoNGPESTLE, PEST, PESTE,
content: This paper examines the evolution and critique of the PESTEL framework (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Ecological, Legal) and its variants for macro-environment analyses. Variants include DESTEP, ETPS, LoNGPESTLE, PEST, PESTE, PESTEC, PESTEL, PESTLE, PESTLED, PESTLEEG, PESTLIED, SLEPT, SPELIT, STEEP, STEEPLE, STEEPLED, STEEPV, STEEPVL, STEPE, STIRDEEPER, TEEPSE, TELOS and probably many more. Initially developed within the field of strategic management of firms, the framework has gained prominence due to its simplicity and pedagogical utility. The framework is often applied in combination with other frameworks, such as scenarios, SWOT analyses, horizon scanning, and Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM). The PESTEL framework has demonstrated its adaptability to different fields and scholarly communities, including foresight and energy policy analyses. However, despite its popularity, the PESTEL framework has been criticised in the field of strategic management for being a simplistic checklist that lacks rigorous analytical depth. Using a systematic literature review, the paper investigates what insights can be gained regarding the transfer and adaptation of the PESTEL framework – and its variants - from the field of strategic management to other fields of research and application, particularly policy-oriented research in the energy domain. The study reveals patterns in the use of acronyms and highlights how to address critiques and limitations of the framework raised within the strategic management literature. Finally, the paper draws implications for scholars using the framework in policy-oriented studies as well as for journal editors and manuscript reviewers.

title: Multi-parameter optimization of Mn(II) adsorption onto KOH-activated Pinus roxburghii biochar using Box-Behnken methodology
summary: Manganese contamination in drinking water poses a significant environmental and public health concern, particularly in regions impacted by industrial discharges and geogenic leaching. This study investigates the potential of activated bioch
content: Manganese contamination in drinking water poses a significant environmental and public health concern, particularly in regions impacted by industrial discharges and geogenic leaching. This study investigates the potential of activated biochar derived from Pinus roxburghii pinecones (PCB), an abundant forestry residue, as a sustainable and cost-effective adsorbent for the removal of Mn(II) from aqueous systems. The biochar was chemically activated using potassium hydroxide to enhance its adsorption properties. Comprehensive characterization using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) confirmed the development of a highly porous structure and the presence of oxygen-containing functional groups responsible for metal binding. To optimize the adsorption process, Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on a Box–Behnken Design (BBD) was employed, considering key operational parameters such as pH, adsorbent dosage, stirring speed, and contact time. The optimal conditions were determined to be pH 8.0, adsorbent dosage of 5 g/L, stirring speed of 230 rpm, and contact time of 45.6 min. Under these conditions, a maximum Mn(II) removal efficiency of 83.59% was achieved. The developed quadratic regression model demonstrated strong predictive capability, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.9614. The findings highlight the effectiveness of pinecone-derived activated biochar as a low-cost and environmentally sustainable adsorbent for manganese removal. This approach not only supports efficient water remediation but also aligns with circular economy principles through the valorization of forestry waste. Graphical abstract

title: Financial Flood Risk Exposure of Nikkei 225 Companies: An Industry Sector and Regional Facility-Scale Perspective
source: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science
summary: Abstract Publicly listed companies are increasingly disclosing climate-related financial risks to their businesses since the promulgation of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), and more recently under the climate
content: Abstract Publicly listed companies are increasingly disclosing climate-related financial risks to their businesses since the promulgation of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), and more recently under the climate-related disclosures issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB). Hence, financial risk exposures associated with geographically-distributed operations and business activities will need to be quantified and benchmarked. While extant research on individual companies or facilities has been available, no prior methodologies have explored these systemic risks based on industry sector classification in the context of listed indices. In this study, we analyzed the characteristics of corporate financial flood risks across regions and industry sectors for the constituent components in the Nikkei 225 Index, representing 225 companies and more than 18,000 facilities. The modeling approach integrates hydrological datasets with multiple climate models and financial records of corporations and facilities. Using estimated property damage (using plant, property, and equipment or PP&E investment proxies) and revenue losses at the facility, corporate, and industry scales, the expected annual damage (EAD) exceeds USD 8.2 billion by 2030. Approximately 60% of losses is derived from property damage to Asian-based facilities, while business interruption losses are driven by European and Asian operations. When benchmarked to earnings, several sectors and companies with high capital asset valuations, including utilities, information technology, consumer discretionary, and industrials show loss ranges exceeding 5%. While financial flood risk was not weighted based on index component allocations, sectors with high fixed asset investments and business interruption losses expose the index to significant impact from extreme weather events.

title: A Study on Addressing Weaknesses and Enhancing Synergy in Sichuan’s Advanced Manufacturing Industry Chain
source: International Journal of Global Economics and Management
summary: Global industrial chains are currently undergoing a restructuring cycle. Compounded by multiple pressures such as geopolitical conflicts and technological containment, the resilience and level of autonomy and control of advanced manufacturi
content: Global industrial chains are currently undergoing a restructuring cycle. Compounded by multiple pressures such as geopolitical conflicts and technological containment, the resilience and level of autonomy and control of advanced manufacturing supply chains have become key factors in competition among major powers. Sichuan, as a core industrial hub in western China, is seizing the opportunity presented by the development of the Chengdu-Chongqing Dual-City Economic Circle. By focusing on “building the circle and strengthening the chain,” the province is driving the transformation of its advanced manufacturing sector toward clustering, high-end development, intelligent manufacturing, and green development. This paper integrates multidisciplinary theories from industrial engineering, complex networks, supply chain resilience, and collaborative governance to establish a three-dimensional “structure–process–collaboration” evaluation framework. Combining entropy-weighted TOPSIS, grey correlation analysis, and MATLAB simulation tools, it conducts comprehensive assessments and scenario simulations of Sichuan’s key industrial chains, including electronic information, aerospace, equipment manufacturing, and new materials for lithium batteries. The results indicate that Sichuan’s manufacturing sector has a solid foundation and industrial clusters have begun to take shape; however, shortcomings remain, including reliance on external core technologies, insufficient coordination between upstream and downstream sectors, and an uneven distribution of regional resources. As the province enters the initial phase of the 15th Five-Year Plan, it needs to optimize the layout of industrial networks, establish digital empowerment platforms, support key enterprises along industrial chains, and improve mechanisms for sharing benefits. These measures will continuously enhance the risk resilience and overall competitiveness of industrial chains, thereby providing decision-making support for fostering new-quality productive forces and building a manufacturing powerhouse.

title: A Novel Distribution Network Reconfiguration Method with the Power Forecasting of DGs
summary: As the development and utilization of renewable energy increase, more distributed generators (DGs) are employed in distribution systems. When a line fault occurs, the inherent intermittency and randomness of DGs’ power are a challenge for d
content: As the development and utilization of renewable energy increase, more distributed generators (DGs) are employed in distribution systems. When a line fault occurs, the inherent intermittency and randomness of DGs’ power are a challenge for distribution network reconfiguration. In this paper, to reduce the influence of power uncertainty, a novel fault reconfiguration method is proposed with the power forecasting of DGs. First, a hybrid power forecasting method is proposed to predict the short-term power of DGs. The history power data of DGs are decomposed by the VMD method, and the decomposition signals are inputted into the TCN-LSTM method. The learning factor and penalty coefficient of TCN-LSTM are optimized by the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) to acquire better prediction results. Then, according to the prediction values of DGs, a fault reconfiguration method is constructed with maximum power restoration and minimum network losses, where the switch operation counts and island operation are taken into account. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The VMD-SSA-TCN-LSTM method has a better performance than traditional forecasting methods in short-term prediction. The proposed fault reconfiguration method can restore the non-fault line load effectively and is suitable for multi-line fault conditions.

title: Green Chemical Engineering for a Net-Zero Future: Integrating Circular Economy Principles with a Sustainable Process Design
summary: Abstract The growing urgency to achieve climate neutrality and resource-efficient industrial development has positioned green and low-carbon chemical engineering at the center of global sustainability efforts. Although significant advances
content: Abstract The growing urgency to achieve climate neutrality and resource-efficient industrial development has positioned green and low-carbon chemical engineering at the center of global sustainability efforts. Although significant advances have been made in circular economy (CE) strategies, renewable feedstocks, carbon management, and process decarbonization, these developments are often examined independently, resulting in a fragmented understanding of their collective potential for sustainable chemical manufacturing. This perspective addresses this gap by providing an integrated assessment of CE principles and low-carbon process engineering strategies that support the transition from conventional linear production systems to circular and carbon-neutral manufacturing frameworks. The perspective examines key CE approaches, including material circularity, industrial symbiosis, resource recovery, and circular product design, alongside challenges related to technological maturity, economic feasibility, and industrial implementation. Recent advances in renewable and circular feedstocks, including biomass, agroindustrial residues, plastic waste, captured CO2, and waste gases, are critically evaluated as alternative carbon resources. Low-carbon process design strategies such as process intensification, electrification, heat integration, and hybrid thermal-electrochemical systems are assessed with respect to their decarbonization potential, scalability, and industrial relevance. The perspective further analyzes developments in green catalysis, photocatalysis, electrocatalysis, biocatalysis, sustainable separation technologies, and circular bioprocessing systems. Particular emphasis is placed on carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), green hydrogen integration, renewable energy deployment, and digitalization through machine learning, digital twins, and real-time process optimization. The complementary roles of life-cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA) are also discussed as essential tools for evaluating environmental and economic sustainability. Unlike previous perspectives that focus on individual technological domains, this Perspective provides a unified framework linking circular economy principles, low-carbon technologies, carbon management, and digital intelligence within a single roadmap for carbon-neutral chemical manufacturing. The synthesis identifies critical technological bottlenecks, implementation challenges, and future research priorities while highlighting opportunities for cross-sector integration and industrial deployment. The findings provide actionable insights for researchers, industry practitioners, and policymakers seeking to accelerate the transition toward resilient, resource-efficient, and low-carbon chemical production systems.

title: Structural Isomerism Modulates CO2 Conversion by Aluminum Germylenoid: A DFT Study
summary: Abstract The CO2 conversion mediated by low-valent main group compounds represents a sustainable strategy for carbon neutrality. Herein, we present a comprehensive DFT study of the reactivity of two kinetically persistent isomers of aluminu
content: Abstract The CO2 conversion mediated by low-valent main group compounds represents a sustainable strategy for carbon neutrality. Herein, we present a comprehensive DFT study of the reactivity of two kinetically persistent isomers of aluminum germylenoid (H2GeAlCl3) toward CO2. Unlike previous studies focusing on monomeric species, we elucidate how the geometric configuration dictates the divergent reaction pathways. Five distinct channels leading to two valuable products (CO and HCOOH) were mapped on the potential-energy surface. Crucially, we identified that the three-membered-ring isomer exhibited the lowest barrier for the formation of HCOOH within the present computational model, establishing it as the kinetically preferred pathway (Path C).

title: From carbon to citizens – integrating energy poverty into the assessment of EU climate neutrality strategies
summary: Extended abstract 4-259-26 Policymakers often lack common frameworks to systematically assess the social, economic, and environmental impacts of energy efficiency (EE) and renewable energy supply (RES) on a level playing field. The SEED MIC
content: Extended abstract 4-259-26 Policymakers often lack common frameworks to systematically assess the social, economic, and environmental impacts of energy efficiency (EE) and renewable energy supply (RES) on a level playing field. The SEED MICAT project addresses this by providing an integrated assessment framework for EU, national, and local governance scales. This framework uses impact coefficients to link technology-specific inputs to multiple indicators through three main steps: quantifying impacts in physical terms, monetizing them where possible, and including them into cost-benefit analysis. The framework supports both ex-ante and ex-post evaluations throughout the entire policy cycle. Designed for high user-friendliness, the methodology requires only a minimal set of mandatory inputs, specifically energy savings for EE actions and installed capacity for RES options. While default values are provided for use in data-scarce environments, users can enter optional data to enhance the accuracy of the results. A key social impact of EE and RES that can be quantified within the framework is energy poverty (EP) alleviation. At the core of the methodology is the estimation of the financial benefit accruing to households (HH) as a result of implemented EE actions and/or deployed RES and its subsequent comparison with the energy poverty gap (EPG) (i.e., the difference between a HH’s absolute or relative energy expenditure and a national EP threshold value). Households for which energy cost savings exceed their EPG are considered lifted out of EP. For this micro-level assessment, aggregated user inputs are disaggregated to determine average costs and benefits per household. This requires simplifying assumptions regarding technologies/actions, their distribution across building types and population groups, and the sharing of investment costs and benefits at building level. For RES deployment, EP impacts are quantified for rooftop PV, assuming proportionally distributed deployment across building types and ubiquitous participation by building residents. Prosumed (owners) or substituted (tenants) electricity is monetized using day-ahead prices or a fixed proportion of retail market prices. Key limitations include the use of national averages as default parameters and the lack of more granular or up-to-date data. Read the full abstract. Download presentation.

title: Advancing municipal decarbonization planning through a scenario-based decision support tool
summary: Extended abstract 5-053-26 Promoting carbon neutrality (CN) in the residential and commercial sectors requires local governments to play an important role; however, it is not easy for each municipality to independently grasp the current sta
content: Extended abstract 5-053-26 Promoting carbon neutrality (CN) in the residential and commercial sectors requires local governments to play an important role; however, it is not easy for each municipality to independently grasp the current state of energy consumption or to formulate and evaluate the effects of CN promotion measures. There has been no framework that enables municipal staff, even without specialised knowledge in the energy field, to consistently and simply conduct analyses ranging from understanding current energy consumption to estimating the effects of various CN promotion measures. In our previous study, we therefore proposed the concept of a tool that enables municipalities to easily grasp their current energy consumption and estimate the effects of CN promotion measures. In this study, based on the above concept, we implemented a web-based software tool that operates in a web browser and outputs slide-format materials for any municipality in Japan. The tool integrates national electricity statistics, census data, and demographic projections with a regional energy demand simulation model. It presents both the current status of CO2 emissions derived from energy use in the selected municipality and projected future CO2 emissions based on various scenarios. The generated slides sequentially explain baseline demand, modelling assumptions, and scenario results. Using this tool, we estimated the CO2 reduction effects of adopting CN promotion measures in the residential sector for three municipalities in Japan. In the scenario analysis, changes in the number of households up to 2050 were taken into account, and two scenarios were assumed for residential CO2 emissions: a Business-as-Usual (BAU) scenario and a CN promotion scenario involving the active implementation of CN promotion measures. The CN promotion scenario included electrification of heating and hot water supply, expansion of photovoltaic (PV) systems, improvements in insulation performance, and appliance efficiency enhancement. By 2050, CO2 emissions under the CN promotion scenario were approximately 56–75% of those under the BAU scenario. Among the individual measures, electrification and photovoltaic (PV) deployment had particularly large effects, and this tendency was common to all three municipalities. Read the full abstract. title: Design and economic analysis of novel solar-nuclear hybrid systems for power generation and hydrogen production
summary: In this study, a novel hybrid solar-nuclear power generation and hydrogen production system (SNPH) is proposed, which consists of a tower-type concentrating solar thermal collector system, a nuclear reactor, a supercritical CO 2 Brayton cyc
content: In this study, a novel hybrid solar-nuclear power generation and hydrogen production system (SNPH) is proposed, which consists of a tower-type concentrating solar thermal collector system, a nuclear reactor, a supercritical CO 2 Brayton cycle, and an alkaline electrolyzer for hydrogen production. This system adopts a parallel heat-source configuration. The overall system is modeled and debugged for optimization using MATLAB. The results show that, under the same boundary condition constraints, the parallel layout of heat sources used in this system outperforms the conventional tandem layout of heat sources, and has a maximum power generation of 148.7 MW at a split ratio of 0.63, corresponding to a thermoelectric efficiency of 40.74%. Then, the thermal energy distribution between the nuclear heat exchanger and molten-salt heat exchanger is adjusted to quantify the corresponding variations in net power output, hydrogen production power, and thermoelectric conversion efficiency, and the maximum hydrogen production rate and power generation were 711.2 kg/h and 161.4 MW, respectively. Next, the system's economic viability was analyzed, and the results showed that the optimal LCOE and LCOH were 0.15$/kWh and 6.315$/kg, respectively. Finally, exergy analysis was conducted on the system, and it was found that the sodium-cooled fast reactor exhibits the largest exergy destruction, followed by the tower-type concentrated solar thermal field, and the exergy efficiency of the condenser was the lowest. This study offers a new paradigm for the design of multi-heat-source multi-energy complementary systems.

title: The Impact of Cloud Technologies In International Business Operations Through Digital Transformation
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic imperative for firms operating across national borders. Among digital infrastructures, cloud computing plays a critical role in enabling multinational enterprises to coordinate global operations
content: Digital transformation has become a strategic imperative for firms operating across national borders. Among digital infrastructures, cloud computing plays a critical role in enabling multinational enterprises to coordinate global operations, manage regulatory heterogeneity, and enhance strategic agility. Despite growing scholarly attention, research on cloud technologies remains fragmented across disciplines and lacks systematic synthesis from an International Business perspective. This study adopts a PRISMA-based systematic literature review of 50 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2024 to examine how cloud-enabled digital transformation influences international business operations. The findings reveal five dominant themes: global operational agility, strategic alignment and performance, governance and regulatory compliance, innovation and ESG outcomes, and risks associated with cross-border cloud adoption. The study contributes to International Business theory by integrating digital infrastructure into discussions of multinational governance and internationalization, and offers managerial and policy implications for navigating digital transformation in global markets.

title: Renewable Energy Generation & Policy for Climate Change
summary: The world is now facing two critical challenges: one is increasing energy demand, and the other is climate change. Both issues are interrelated. Policymakers need to think carefully about both issues so that a better policy can be followed
tags: Environmental impact of the energy industry
content: The world is now facing two critical challenges: one is increasing energy demand, and the other is climate change. Both issues are interrelated. Policymakers need to think carefully about both issues so that a better policy can be followed for solving both problems. In this paper, different ways will be explored through which both issues can be addressed. These ways include the renewable energy resources such as solar and wind energy, along with nuclear energy. New material sciences technologies, such as new materials for energy storage, radionuclide management from nuclear power, and the ecological footprint of renewable energy infrastructure, will all be critically examined. This paper examines global policy efforts, case studies, and technological advancements to highlight the importance of coordinated actions in accelerating the transition to cleaner energy systems and effectively combating climate change.

title: Photoelectrocatalysis on TiO2 Derived from Titanium Acetylacetonate: Effect of Decomposition Temperature
source: BULLETIN OF CHEMICAL REACTION ENGINEERING AND CATALYSIS
summary: Photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) water splitting utilizing titanium dioxide (TiO2) photoanodes presents a promising avenue for sustainable hydrogen production. Understanding the correlation linking the synthesis conditions to structural and phas
content: Photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) water splitting utilizing titanium dioxide (TiO2) photoanodes presents a promising avenue for sustainable hydrogen production. Understanding the correlation linking the synthesis conditions to structural and phase evolution of semiconductor materials, which is essential for the development of photoanodes with improved PEC activity, remains challenging. This study aims to elucidate the structure- and phase-dependent PEC activity of TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs) obtained via the non-isothermal decomposition of titanium oxyacetylacetonate (TiO(acac)₂) precursor at varying final temperatures (Tfin). The microstructural parameters and phase composition of the TiO2 NPs were determined via Rietveld refinement of X-ray diffraction (XRD) data. The PEC activity of spin-coated TiO2/FTO photoanodes was evaluated via open-circuit potential (OCP) measurements, OCP decay, and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) under chopped illumination. The results indicate that the anatase-rutile ratio and crystallite dimensions can be modulated by varying Tfin in the range of 500-700 °C. An optimized mixed-phase TiO2 comprising 71.7% anatase and 28.3% rutile, with the crystallite sizes Dav of 29.6 nm and 55.6 nm, respectively, is achieved at 650 °C enabling an efficient transition to free-electron transport and maximized photoactivity. These findings offer essential design principles for managing structural and phase transformations in TiO2-based photoanodes via the metal-organic decomposition route.
